amsa-308.key: Markus is haemodynamically stable and not hypoxic, with no signs of heart failure, shock or a murmur. However, he is pale and sweaty, his ischaemic-type pain is ongoing, and his heart rate and BP are rising, so he needs analgesia, nitrates and a repeat ECG now. His arm BPs and radial pulses are equal and his pain is not reproduced on palpation, which makes aortic dissection and chest wall pain less likely. A normal examination does not exclude an acute coronary syndrome.

amsa-310.vitals: HR 84 bpm regular, BP 118/74 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C, weight 78 kg, height 165 cm (BMI 28.7 kg/m^2), pain 7/10
amsa-310.general: Comfortable at rest, alert and speaking in full sentences, a bit anxious. Walks in with a slight limp to the left. Not breathless, pale or sweaty. Overweight. Mild acne on the face. No peripheral cyanosis.

steps.do: Exposes both legs from groin to toes and compares the two sides for swelling, colour, redness, skin breaks, bites, bruising and collateral superficial veins.
steps.find: Left calf visibly swollen compared with the right. No redness, streaking, skin breaks, insect bites or bruising. No visible collateral (non-varicose) superficial veins. Both feet pink.

steps.do: Uses the back of the hand to compare temperature on both legs, then palpates gently along the deep veins of the calf, popliteal fossa and thigh on each side.
steps.find: Left calf slightly warmer than the right. Tender along the deep veins of the left calf and in the left popliteal fossa. No tenderness along the femoral vein in the thigh. Right leg not tender.

steps.do: Presses firmly for a few seconds over the ankles and lower shins on both sides, looking for pitting.
steps.find: Pitting oedema of the left ankle and lower shin. No oedema on the right.

steps.do: Measures calf circumference on both sides 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity, and compares thigh circumference.
steps.find: Calf circumference left 39.5 cm, right 36.0 cm (3.5 cm larger on the left). Thigh circumference the same on both sides, so the whole leg is not swollen.

steps.do: Palpates the left popliteal fossa for a mass or cyst and examines the knee for effusion and range of movement.
steps.find: No mass or cyst felt in the popliteal fossa. Knee has full range of movement, with no effusion.

steps.do: Palpates the gastrocnemius and soleus for a defect, tests resisted plantarflexion, does the Simmonds-Thompson test and watches her bear weight and walk.
steps.find: No palpable defect in the calf muscles. Mild pain on resisted plantarflexion. Simmonds-Thompson test normal (Achilles intact). Bears weight with a slight antalgic limp.

steps.do: Palpates the femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both sides, checks capillary refill, and tests sensation and power in both feet.
steps.find: All pulses present and equal on both sides. Capillary refill under 2 seconds on both sides. Sensation and power normal in both legs.

steps.do: Palpates the inguinal lymph nodes on both sides.
steps.find: No inguinal lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Checks the JVP, auscultates the heart and both lung fields, and looks for a pleural rub.
steps.find: JVP not raised. Heart sounds dual with no added sounds and no loud P2. Chest clear with normal breath sounds throughout and no pleural rub.

bedside.find: Negative.
Normal: no blood, protein, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.4 mmol/L.
Sinus rhythm at 84 bpm, normal axis, normal intervals. No right heart strain pattern (no S1Q3T3, no right bundle branch block, no T-wave inversion in V1 to V4).

amsa-310.key: Mary has a swollen, warm left calf that is 3.5 cm bigger than the right, with pitting oedema and tenderness along the deep veins. That gives a Wells score of 3 (DVT likely), so she goes straight to compression ultrasound rather than a D-dimer. Her pulses are normal, there is no defect in the calf muscle, no cyst behind the knee and no redness or skin break, which makes arterial disease, a muscle tear, a Baker's cyst and cellulitis less likely. Her observations, chest examination and ECG are normal, so there are no clinical signs of PE, and with a negative pregnancy test she is stable for outpatient workup.

amsa-323.vitals: 14:00: Temp 37.5 °C, HR 92 bpm regular, BP 126/78 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air, capillary BGL 5.4 mmol/L, pain 3/10. Weight 82 kg, height 180 cm (BMI 25.3 kg/m²).
amsa-323.general: Comfortable lying still in bed. Alert, fully oriented and talking in full sentences, not drowsy. Not pale, jaundiced or flushed. Peripheral cannula in the left forearm with a clean site and nothing running.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes and check capillary refill.
steps.find: Mucous membranes slightly dry. Capillary refill 2 seconds. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Assess mouth opening, dentition, neck movement and Mallampati class.
steps.find: Good mouth opening. All his own teeth, none loose, no caps or crowns. Full neck movement. Mallampati class 1.

steps.do: Palpate the pulse and auscultate the heart.
steps.find: Pulse 92 and regular. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs.

steps.do: Auscultate the chest.
steps.find: Good air entry on both sides. Chest clear, no added sounds.

steps.do: Inspect with the patient lying flat and the abdomen exposed.
steps.find: Not distended. No scars. Abdomen moves normally with breathing.

steps.do: Palpate gently, starting in the left upper quadrant away from the pain, then deeper. Check Rovsing's and Murphy's signs, feel for a mass and examine the liver and spleen.
steps.find: Tender in the right iliac fossa, worst at McBurney's point, with mild voluntary guarding there. Rovsing's sign positive. The rest of the abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no rigidity and no generalised peritonism. No palpable mass. No hepatosplenomegaly. Murphy's sign negative.

steps.do: Percuss for tenderness and listen for bowel sounds.
steps.find: Percussion tenderness in the right iliac fossa only. Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.do: Palpate the renal angles and examine the inguinal and femoral hernial orifices.
steps.find: Renal angles non-tender. Hernial orifices clear.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both calves.
steps.find: Both calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling.

steps.do: Offer a genital and digital rectal examination with a chaperone.
steps.find: The examiner says it is not needed today.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L.
Negative for blood, leucocytes, nitrites and protein. Trace ketones, which fits his poor intake since yesterday.
Not needed before an anaesthetic in a well 38-year-old with no cardiac history or symptoms.

amsa-323.key: Michael has tenderness and mild guarding in the right iliac fossa, worst at McBurney's point, with percussion tenderness and a positive Rovsing's sign. The rest of his abdomen is soft with no rigidity, which fits localised appendicitis rather than a perforation with generalised peritonitis. His low-grade temperature and heart rate of 92 show no sepsis or organ dysfunction, but his mucous membranes are slightly dry after a long fast, so he needs IV fluids. His airway, heart and chest are normal, his calves are soft and his urine dipstick shows no blood, so nothing stops him going for a general anaesthetic and a urinary cause is less likely.

amsa-355.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 96% on room air, BP 132/78 mmHg, HR 104 bpm regular, temperature 38.8 °C, CRT 2 seconds, pain 0/10, BGL 6.1 mmol/L, weight 68 kg
amsa-355.general: Woman, 68, lying still on the trolley. She is flushed and warm to touch, slow to respond and not distressed. She pauses before answering and loses the thread of long questions. Mucous membranes are dry. Monitoring is attached.

steps.do: Score the GCS by component, using best eye, verbal and motor response.
steps.find: GCS 14. Eyes open spontaneously (E4), conversation confused (V4), obeys commands (M6).

steps.do: Do the 4AT: alertness, AMT4 (age, date of birth, place, year), months of the year backwards, and acute change or fluctuating course from the collateral history.
steps.find: 4AT 7. Alertness normal (0). AMT4: age and date of birth correct, but she thinks she is 'at the school' and gets the year wrong (2 errors, scores 2). Months backwards: stops after 4 months (1). Acute change reported by her partner (4).

steps.do: Check for neck stiffness, Kernig's sign and photophobia, and inspect the whole skin for a rash, petechiae or vesicles.
steps.find: No neck stiffness. Kernig's sign negative. No photophobia. No rash, petechiae or vesicles anywhere.

steps.do: Look for a head injury. Do otoscopy, inspect the mouth, teeth and lips, and palpate the sinuses.
steps.find: No sign of head injury. Tympanic membranes normal. Teeth fine with no abscess. Sinuses not tender. Mucous membranes dry. No active cold sore on the lips.

steps.do: Check pupils, fundoscopy, eye movements, visual fields, facial symmetry and speech.
steps.find: Pupils 3 mm, equal and reactive. No papilloedema. Eye movements full, visual fields grossly full, face symmetrical. Speech clear with no dysarthria, but slow, with occasional pauses to find a word.

steps.do: Check tone, power, pronator drift, reflexes, sensation and coordination (finger-nose) on both sides.
steps.find: Tone normal. Power 4/5 throughout the right arm and 5/5 on the left. Right pronator drift. Biceps and triceps reflexes brisker on the right. Light touch reduced over the right hand and forearm. Finger-nose slow on the right, in keeping with the weakness.

steps.do: Check tone, power, reflexes, sensation and plantar responses on both sides.
steps.find: Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and equal on both sides. Plantars flexor on both sides.

steps.do: Feel the pulse, listen to the heart and check the monitor rhythm.
steps.find: Pulse 104, regular. Heart sounds dual with no murmur. Monitor shows sinus rhythm.

steps.do: Listen to the chest. Palpate the abdomen and look for signs of liver disease.
steps.find: Chest clear. Abdomen soft and non-tender. No hepatomegaly and no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the hands and joints.
steps.find: Long-standing rheumatoid changes: ulnar deviation at the MCP joints. No active synovitis.

bedside.find: 6.1 mmol/L (normal)
Negative for leucocytes and nitrites
Sinus tachycardia, 104 bpm

amsa-355.key: Jane is 68 and immunosuppressed. She has fever (38.8 °C, HR 104) and new confusion (GCS 14, 4AT 7) with a normal BGL. Her right arm shows upper motor neurone and sensory signs, and she has word-finding pauses. Together these point to a left-sided brain process, and with fever that means encephalitis, most likely herpes simplex encephalitis. Normal results for meningism, rash, papilloedema, ears, sinuses, teeth, urine and chest make the other causes less likely, but she is on methotrexate and steroids, so aciclovir must start now and Listeria must still be covered. The focal deficit, reduced GCS and immunosuppression mean a CT brain before the LP.

amsa-357.vitals: HR 88/min irregularly irregular, BP 158/86 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 36.7 °C, alert, capillary glucose 6.4 mmol/L
amsa-357.general: Alert, comfortable and not distressed, sitting in the chair beside his bed and chatty. Average build (82 kg). No facial asymmetry. Pupils look equal, no ptosis. No rashes or scars on the face or scalp.

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate and rhythm, auscultate the heart and listen over both carotids
steps.find: Pulse 88/min, irregularly irregular (possible atrial fibrillation). Heart sounds dual, no murmur. No carotid bruits.

steps.do: Ask about any change in smell
steps.find: No change in smell or taste.

steps.do: Snellen acuity in each eye separately, using a pinhole as he has no distance glasses; Ishihara plates in each eye
steps.find: Acuity 6/9 right, 6/9 left. All Ishihara plates read correctly with each eye.

steps.do: Confrontation fields at about 1 m, each eye tested separately, all four quadrants; red pin near fixation to test for central sparing and map the blind spot
steps.find: Right eye misses the target in the upper and lower left (nasal) quadrants. Left eye misses it in the upper and lower left (temporal) quadrants. Right half-field normal in each eye. The defect stops at the vertical midline. A red pin is still seen about 5 degrees left of fixation in each eye. Right blind spot the same size as the examiner's. Left blind spot lies inside the missing half-field and cannot be mapped. With both eyes open he misses the target anywhere on the left. This is a left homonymous hemianopia with central sparing.

steps.do: Ophthalmoscopy of both eyes
steps.find: Clear media with lens implants. Optic discs pink with sharp margins, no swelling. Mild arteriolar narrowing and arteriovenous nipping. No haemorrhages, exudates or emboli.

steps.do: Pupil size, direct and consensual light reflexes, swinging light test, accommodation, eye movements in an H pattern, asking about diplopia and watching for nystagmus
steps.find: Pupils 3 mm, equal and round. Direct and consensual reflexes normal. No relative afferent pupillary defect. Accommodation normal. Eye movements full with smooth pursuit, no diplopia, no nystagmus.

steps.do: Pinprick and light touch in V1 to V3 on both sides; palpate the masseters while he clenches; jaw opening against resistance and side to side; jaw jerk; mention the corneal reflex
steps.find: Sensation normal and symmetrical. Masseters of normal bulk, contracting equally. Jaw opens strongly without deviating and moves normally side to side. Jaw jerk present, not brisk. Corneal reflex would be present on both sides.

steps.do: Raise the eyebrows, close the eyes tightly against resistance, puff out the cheeks, smile, pout
steps.find: Forehead wrinkles symmetrically, eye closure strong, cheeks hold air, smile symmetrical, pout normal. No facial weakness.

steps.do: Listen to the voice, watch the palate and uvula on 'ah', ask for a cough, mention the gag; shoulder shrug and head turn against resistance; inspect the tongue, then protrusion and side-to-side movement
steps.find: Voice normal, not hoarse. Palate rises symmetrically, uvula central, cough strong, gag would be present. Shrug and head turn strong and equal. Tongue of normal bulk, no fasciculations, protrudes in the midline and moves normally. (CN VIII not required; hearing normal to conversation.)

steps.do: Limb tone, power, reflexes, sensation, pronator drift, coordination, tactile inattention, speech and gait
steps.find: Tone, power 5/5, reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical in all four limbs. Plantars flexor. No pronator drift. Finger-nose and heel-shin normal. No extinction on touching both sides at once. Speech fluent, no dysarthria or dysphasia. Aware of his visual problem. Gait steady.

bedside.find: 6.4 mmol/L, so hypoglycaemia is not the cause
Irregularly irregular rhythm with no P waves, ventricular rate about 90/min, no ST changes: atrial fibrillation (formal ECG given in Part 2)
Passed. Voice normal, no cough or wet voice on water sips.

amsa-357.key: Testing each eye separately shows a congruous left homonymous hemianopia that stops at the vertical midline and spares central vision. Acuity, colour vision and pupils are normal and there is no RAPD, so the lesion is behind the chiasm on the right, most likely in the occipital cortex, and is not an eye problem. There is no weakness, sensory loss or neglect, which points to the posterior rather than the middle cerebral artery, and the irregularly irregular pulse suggests atrial fibrillation as the embolic source.

amsa-374.vitals: HR 96/min regular, BP 144/84 mmHg (right arm), RR 26/min, SpO2 92% on room air, temperature 36.8 °C, pain 5/10 (repeat set at 09:55)
amsa-374.general: Overweight man sitting upright on the trolley, pale and a little sweaty, with a hand on the centre of his chest. He speaks in short phrases and pauses to catch his breath. Mild accessory muscle use. Alert and appropriate. No cyanosis. No xanthelasma. On the cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, feel peripheral temperature and measure capillary refill
steps.find: Peripheries warm. CRT 2 seconds. No peripheral cyanosis, no clubbing, no tar staining.

steps.do: Palpate both radial pulses together for rate, rhythm, volume and radio-radial delay, then compare the femoral pulses
steps.find: Radial pulse 96/min, regular, normal volume. Radial pulses equal with no radio-radial delay. Femoral pulses present and equal.

steps.do: Measure the BP in the right and left arms
steps.find: Right arm 144/84 mmHg, left arm 140/82 mmHg. No significant difference between the arms.

steps.do: Inspect the eyes and mouth, and assess the JVP with him sitting up
steps.find: No xanthelasma, no central cyanosis. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the praecordium for the apex beat and heaves, then auscultate all areas
steps.find: Apex beat not displaced, no heaves or thrills. Dual heart sounds, no added sounds, no murmurs (no aortic stenosis or mitral regurgitation murmur), no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check the trachea, expansion, percussion and auscultation front and back
steps.find: Trachea central. Hyperexpanded chest with equal but reduced expansion. Resonant to percussion on both sides. Vesicular breath sounds, reduced throughout but equal, with a prolonged expiratory phase. No wheeze, no crackles at the bases.

steps.do: Palpate the sternum, costochondral junctions and chest wall
steps.find: No tenderness. Pressing does not bring on the pain.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen, including the epigastrium, and feel for an aortic mass
steps.find: Soft, non-tender, no epigastric tenderness, no pulsatile mass. Well-healed right inguinal hernia scar.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the calves and check for pitting oedema
steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling or asymmetry, no pitting oedema.

bedside.find: 11.2 mmol/L (raised; known insulin-treated type 2 diabetes)
Sinus rhythm 94 to 96/min, no ectopics or arrhythmia seen
Recorded at 09:45 while he had pain. The examiner gives it in Part 2.
Cannula in place. Bloods including hs-troponin, FBC, EUC, coagulation and lipids sent at 09:45. Results given in Part 2.
SpO2 92% on room air, within his COPD target of 88 to 92%

amsa-374.key: Bill is pale, sweaty, tachypnoeic and speaking in short phrases, but he is haemodynamically stable and well perfused. He has no signs of heart failure (JVP not raised, no crackles, no oedema), no murmur and no pericardial rub, which suggests ongoing ischaemia rather than a complication of it. Equal radial pulses and arm BPs, equal femoral pulses and no pulsatile mass argue against aortic dissection. Soft calves, a non-tender chest wall and a soft abdomen make PE, a musculoskeletal cause and an abdominal cause less likely. His chest is hyperexpanded with reduced but equal air entry, which fits his COPD, but a chest X-ray is still needed to exclude a pneumothorax. His SpO2 of 92% is within his COPD target, so he does not need routine oxygen.

amsa-375.vitals: 09:40: HR 86 beats/min regular, BP 146/92 mmHg, RR 20/min, SpO2 95% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, weight 82 kg (79 kg in the practice record three months ago, so up 3 kg), height 175 cm, BMI 26.8 kg/m²
amsa-375.general: Overweight older man sitting upright in the chair. He is mildly breathless after walking in from the waiting room. This is easing at rest but does not fully settle, and he speaks in full sentences. He is not cyanosed and not pale. He is alert and oriented. No oxygen or walking aids. His Ventolin puffer is with him.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and tar staining, and test for a fine tremor with the arms outstretched
steps.find: Hands warm, capillary refill under 2 seconds. No clubbing, no tar staining, no peripheral cyanosis and no tremor.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm, volume and character, and check for radio-radial delay
steps.find: 86 beats/min and regular. Small in volume and slow-rising. No radio-radial delay.

steps.do: Look for conjunctival pallor, central cyanosis of the lips and tongue, and lid lag
steps.find: No conjunctival pallor, no central cyanosis and no lid lag.

steps.do: With him at 45 degrees, measure the JVP above the sternal angle. Palpate one carotid at a time for character, auscultate both carotids, check the trachea is central and examine for a goitre
steps.find: JVP raised 4 cm above the sternal angle. Carotid pulse small in volume and slow-rising. The systolic murmur is heard over both carotids. Trachea midline. No goitre.

steps.do: Inspect for scars and deformity, locate and characterise the apex beat, and feel for heaves and thrills
steps.find: No scars. Apex beat in the 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line, not displaced. It is forceful and sustained (heaving). No thrill and no parasternal heave.

steps.do: Auscultate all four areas while palpating the carotid. Sit him forward and listen in expiration at the right 2nd intercostal space and the left sternal edge. Follow the murmur to the carotids and the apex
steps.find: Harsh grade 3/6 ejection systolic murmur, late-peaking, loudest at the right 2nd intercostal space. It is louder sitting forward in expiration and radiates to both carotids. It is also heard at the apex, where it sounds more musical. S2 is soft, with A2 barely audible. S4 present. No diastolic murmur.

steps.do: Inspect for hyperinflation, then check expansion, percuss and auscultate both lungs, and test vocal resonance
steps.find: No hyperinflation. Expansion slightly reduced on the right. Fine end-inspiratory crackles at both bases. The right base is stony dull to percussion, with reduced breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance. No wheeze and no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate for hepatomegaly and right upper quadrant tenderness, and check for ascites
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. Liver edge not palpable and no right upper quadrant tenderness. No ascites.

steps.do: Press for pitting oedema at the ankles, shins and sacrum, and inspect and palpate both calves
steps.find: No pitting oedema at the ankles, shins or sacrum. Calves soft, non-tender and equal in size.

bedside.find: 6.1 mmol/L (random)
No protein, blood, glucose, leucocytes or nitrites.
The practice nurse records it at 09:55. The examiner hands it over with the other results in Part 2.

amsa-375.key: He has a slow-rising, small-volume pulse and a harsh, late-peaking ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. With a soft S2, an S4 and a heaving, undisplaced apex, this points to severe aortic stenosis, which fits his exertional chest tightness and exertional syncope. He is also congested: JVP raised 4 cm, fine crackles at both bases, a stony dull right base consistent with a pleural effusion, and 3 kg of weight gain in 3 months. This is heart failure needing same-day hospital care, even though he has no peripheral oedema. There is no wheeze, no hyperinflation and no clubbing, which argues against his asthma or COPD as the cause, so his puffer doesn't help.

amsa-376.vitals: 10:10 on 2 L/min nasal prongs: RR 26/min, SpO2 89%, HR 108 beats/min regular, BP 134/82 mmHg, temperature 38.2 °C, alert (AVPU A)
amsa-376.general: Sitting forward with her hands on her knees (tripod position). She is breathing through pursed lips, speaks in short phrases and is using her neck muscles to breathe. On nasal prongs at 2 L/min from her portable cylinder. During the examination she coughs up a small amount of thick yellow sputum. Alert and oriented. Lips pink, with no central cyanosis.

steps.do: Inspect for cyanosis, clubbing, tar staining and tremor, and feel temperature. Check for a flapping tremor (asterixis) with the arms outstretched and wrists extended.
steps.find: Hands warm. No peripheral cyanosis, no clubbing, no tar staining and no fine tremor. No asterixis.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and character, including a bounding pulse from CO2 retention.
steps.find: 108 beats/min, regular and not bounding.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for central cyanosis and look for pursed-lip breathing.
steps.find: Lips and tongue pink, with no central cyanosis. Pursed-lip breathing.

steps.do: Check tracheal position and cricosternal distance, look for a tracheal tug and accessory muscle use, assess the JVP and palpate for lymph nodes.
steps.find: Trachea central. Cricosternal distance reduced to two finger-breadths, with a tracheal tug. Sternocleidomastoids active. JVP not raised. No lymph nodes.

steps.do: Inspect the shape of the chest and the work of breathing, then assess chest expansion front and back.
steps.find: Barrel chest with an increased front-to-back diameter. Indrawing between the ribs. Expansion reduced but symmetrical.

steps.do: Percuss front, sides and back comparing both sides, including cardiac and liver dullness.
steps.find: Hyper-resonant throughout. Cardiac and liver dullness reduced. No focal dullness.

steps.do: Auscultate front, sides and back, ask her to cough and listen again, and test vocal resonance.
steps.find: Breath sounds reduced throughout with a prolonged expiratory phase and widespread polyphonic expiratory wheeze. Coarse crackles at both bases that change after she coughs. No bronchial breathing and no pleural rub. Vocal resonance equal on both sides.

steps.do: Palpate for a right ventricular heave and auscultate the heart.
steps.find: No right ventricular heave. Heart sounds soft but dual, with no murmur.

steps.do: Check for sacral and ankle oedema, and examine both calves for swelling, tenderness and asymmetry (DVT).
steps.find: No sacral or ankle oedema. Calves soft, equal and non-tender.

bedside.find: A small amount of thick, yellow, purulent sputum. No blood. Potted for microscopy and culture.
6.8 mmol/L (normal).
Requested. The practice nurse records it after the examination, and the result is given in Part 2.
Taken in the practice. The result is given in Part 2.

amsa-376.key: She has severe COPD on home oxygen and is now febrile, tachycardic and tachypnoeic. She is working hard to breathe (tripod position, accessory muscles, intercostal indrawing), and her SpO2 is only 89% on her usual 2 L/min. Her chest shows hyperinflation, widespread wheeze and coarse basal crackles that change with coughing, with no focal dullness or bronchial breathing. Together with her purulent sputum, this points to an infective exacerbation of COPD rather than a pneumonia. There is no asterixis, bounding pulse or drowsiness to suggest CO2 retention, and no raised JVP, oedema or calf signs to suggest heart failure or DVT. Still, a past PE with no anticoagulation and hypoxaemia on her usual oxygen mean she needs hospital assessment, including a blood gas.

amsa-377.vitals: Temp 37.4 °C, HR 108 bpm regular, BP 134/82 mmHg, RR 20/min, SpO2 97% on room air, CRT 3 seconds, pain 8/10 (09:40, on arrival)
amsa-377.general: Uncomfortable man lying very still with his hands on a visibly distended abdomen, grimacing when he shifts. Alert and talking in full sentences. Not pale, not jaundiced. Weight 96 kg, height 178 cm (BMI 30).

steps.do: Look at the tongue and mucous membranes, check skin turgor and capillary refill
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor, central CRT 3 seconds, so clinically dehydrated.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate and rhythm, look for clubbing and palmar pallor, check the conjunctivae and sclerae, palpate the supraclavicular fossae
steps.find: Pulse 108 and regular. No clubbing or palmar pallor. Conjunctivae pink, no scleral jaundice. No supraclavicular lymph nodes (no Virchow's node).

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lung fields
steps.find: Heart sounds dual with no murmurs. Chest clear, good air entry on both sides.

steps.do: Expose the abdomen and inspect from the end of the bed and from the side, look for scars, visible peristalsis and hernias, ask him to cough
steps.find: Grossly and evenly distended abdomen, tense and shiny. Healed right iliac fossa scar (appendicectomy at 15). No visible peristalsis. No hernias seen on coughing. Coughing makes him wince because the abdomen is so tight, but there is no localised cough tenderness.

steps.do: Gentle light then deeper palpation, starting away from the pain, watching his face; check for guarding, rigidity and rebound; feel for masses and organomegaly
steps.find: Tender all over, worst in the left iliac fossa with voluntary guarding there. Mild right iliac fossa tenderness. No rigidity, no rebound tenderness. No mass can be felt through the distension. Liver and spleen not palpable.

steps.do: Percuss all regions, assess percussion tenderness and test for shifting dullness
steps.find: Tympanic (hyper-resonant) throughout. No percussion tenderness. No shifting dullness.

steps.do: Listen for bowel sounds for at least 30 seconds
steps.find: Bowel sounds present, high-pitched and tinkling, consistent with mechanical obstruction.

steps.do: Examine the inguinal and femoral orifices on both sides, at rest and on coughing; examine the scrotum
steps.find: Inguinal and femoral orifices clear on both sides, including on cough. Scrotum normal.

steps.do: Palpate and percuss the renal angles
steps.find: Non-tender on both sides.

steps.do: Offer a digital rectal examination with consent and a chaperone, and inspect the glove
steps.find: Empty rectum with no faeces. No mass felt. No blood or melaena on the glove.

bedside.find: The practice nurse is doing it now; the result is given in Part 2.
Sample collected and with the nurse; the result is given in Part 2.
Not available in the practice; they would be done in hospital (FBC, UEC, lipase, CRP, venous gas with lactate, CT abdomen and pelvis).

amsa-377.key: The abdomen is grossly distended and tympanic, with tinkling bowel sounds and an empty rectum. With early obstipation and late bilious vomiting, this points to mechanical large bowel obstruction. The hernial orifices are clear, and the left iliac fossa tenderness with guarding points to the sigmoid. He has a tachycardia of 108, is clinically dehydrated and has a temperature of 37.4 °C. There is no peritonism, but the mild right iliac fossa tenderness raises concern about caecal distension, and constant pain suggests he may be developing ischaemia. He needs urgent transfer to hospital and close repeat observations.

amsa-379.vitals: RR 16/min, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 158/92 mmHg, HR 92/min irregularly irregular, temperature 36.8 °C, pain 0/10, bedside glucose 8.4 mmol/L
amsa-379.general: Frightened but alert and clear-headed, lying on the trolley. GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). Speaks normally. Central obesity, weight 102 kg. Wet trousers. No injury from the fall and no scalp or head wound. He cannot move his left leg.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse, measure the BP, check the JVP, listen to the heart and carotids, and look at the ankles and calves
steps.find: Pulse 92/min and irregularly irregular. BP 158/92. Heart sounds dual with no murmur. No carotid bruits. JVP not raised. No ankle oedema. Calves soft and non-tender.

steps.do: Listen to the chest
steps.find: Clear on both sides.

steps.do: Assess speech, comprehension, naming, repetition and orientation, and test for visual and sensory inattention
steps.find: Fluent speech with normal comprehension, naming and repetition. No dysarthria. Oriented. No visual or sensory inattention on either side.

steps.do: Test visual fields, pupils, eye movements, facial movement and sensation, palate and tongue
steps.find: Visual fields full to confrontation. Pupils equal and reactive. Eye movements full with no nystagmus. Face symmetrical, with normal movement of the forehead and lower face. Normal facial sensation, palate and tongue.

steps.do: Test pronator drift, tone, power (including shoulder abduction), reflexes, sensation and finger-nose on both sides
steps.find: No pronator drift. Normal tone. Power 5/5 throughout on both sides, including shoulder abduction. Reflexes normal and symmetrical. Normal sensation. Finger-nose normal.

steps.do: Compare tone, power, reflexes, plantar responses and all sensory modalities between the left and right legs
steps.find: Left: tone reduced. Hip flexion 1/5 (a flicker). Hip extension, knee and ankle 0/5. Knee and ankle reflexes present but slightly reduced compared with the right. Plantar extensor (upgoing). Light touch, pinprick, vibration and joint position sense absent from the foot to the groin. Right: normal tone, power 5/5, normal reflexes, plantar flexor, normal sensation.

steps.do: Look for a sensory level on the trunk and test perianal and saddle sensation
steps.find: No sensory level on the trunk. Perianal and saddle sensation intact.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the spine
steps.find: No spinal tenderness or deformity.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen and feel for a bladder (offer a PR if indicated)
steps.find: Abdomen soft. Bladder not palpable. If a PR is offered: normal anal tone and perianal sensation.

steps.do: Ask whether gait can be assessed
steps.find: He cannot stand on the left leg. Do not test, because he would fall.

bedside.find: 8.4 mmol/L (mildly raised, non-fasting, in a known diabetic). Hypoglycaemia is excluded.
60 mL residual after he was changed. No retention.
5 (left leg motor 3, sensory 2, every other item 0).
Recorded. The examiner gives the result in Part 2.

amsa-379.key: The left leg has an acute upper motor neurone deficit (power 1/5 at the hip and 0/5 below, an upgoing plantar despite reduced tone, and loss of all sensation to the groin) with urinary incontinence, while the face, arm, speech, vision and attention are all normal. This localises to the right anterior cerebral artery territory, and the irregularly irregular pulse suggests a cardioembolic source from AF. Normal glucose, intact saddle sensation, no sensory level, no spinal tenderness and an empty bladder make hypoglycaemia and spinal or cauda equina causes unlikely, so this needs a code stroke now.

amsa-392.vitals: Arrival (14:05): HR 75/min regular, BP 152/90 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, BGL 7.4 mmol/L, pain 4/10. After the nurse's report (14:15): HR 84/min irregular (occasional early beats), BP 148/88 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 96% on room air, pain 6/10.
amsa-392.general: Anxious, pale, cool and clammy overweight man (about 92 kg). He is lying propped up on the trolley and holding his left arm. He speaks in full sentences with no increased work of breathing. No xanthelasma. He has an IV cannula in place (inserted by the paramedics) and is on a cardiac monitor.

steps.do: Feel the hands and check capillary refill
steps.find: Cool, sweaty peripheries. Capillary refill 2 seconds.

steps.do: Check rate, rhythm and volume, compare the two radial pulses, check for radio-radial delay and feel the femoral pulses
steps.find: 84/min, irregular because of occasional early beats, normal volume. Radial pulses equal with no radio-radial delay. Femoral pulses equal.

steps.do: Measure the BP in the right arm, then the left arm straight after
steps.find: Right arm 152/90 mmHg, left arm 148/88 mmHg. No significant difference between the arms.

steps.do: Inspect for xanthelasma and pallor, and assess the JVP
steps.find: Pale. No xanthelasma. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Palpate the apex beat, then auscultate all areas for heart sounds, added sounds, murmurs and a rub
steps.find: Apex not displaced. Dual heart sounds with no added sounds (no S3), no murmurs and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Press on the chest wall over the site of the pain
steps.find: Not tender. Pressing does not reproduce the pain.

steps.do: Check the trachea and chest expansion, then percuss and auscultate the lung fields, including the bases
steps.find: Trachea central, equal expansion, resonant to percussion. Vesicular breath sounds with no crackles or wheeze.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate the epigastrium and right upper quadrant, and feel for a pulsatile mass
steps.find: Healed laparoscopic port scars. Soft and non-tender throughout, including the epigastrium and right upper quadrant. No pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the calves and ankles for tenderness, swelling and pitting oedema
steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling and no pitting oedema. Both knees show bony enlargement and crepitus.

bedside.find: 7.4 mmol/L
Sinus rhythm at 75/min on arrival. At 14:15 the rate is 84/min with occasional early (ectopic) beats.
The nurse recorded it at 14:10. The examiner hands it over in Part 2.
With him from 13:35. GTN 400 micrograms sublingual twice and fentanyl 50 micrograms IV, with pain falling from 8/10 to 4/10. No aspirin recorded. Their 12-lead did not transmit.

amsa-392.key: Brad is pale, cool and clammy with ischaemic-sounding pain that is coming back, and new ectopic beats. This is an evolving acute coronary syndrome with a risk of arrhythmia (VF), so he needs a senior, defibrillator pads, a repeat ECG, GTN or titrated analgesia, and aspirin (none given so far). His BP and pulses are equal in both arms and there is no back pain, which argues against aortic dissection. His chest is clear, his JVP is not raised, he has no new murmur and his SpO2 is 96%, so there is no heart failure or mechanical complication (Killip I) and no oxygen is needed. His BP is under 180/110, so it allows both GTN and fibrinolysis.

amsa-412.vitals: RR 26/min, SpO2 91% on room air, HR 108/min irregular, BP 144/86 mmHg, Temp 36.8 °C, CRT 2 s, alert (AVPU A), weight 92 kg (usual about 88 kg)
amsa-412.general: Sitting propped up on the trolley at 45 degrees and unable to lie flat ("I can't lie flat, I'll be gasping"). Mildly breathless at rest, speaking in sentences with pauses. Not cyanosed, not pale, not sweaty. Alert and cooperative, a little worried. Cardiac monitor on and an IV cannula in place. Weight on the ED scales today is 92 kg, about 4 kg above his usual. If he is laid flat, he becomes more breathless and SpO2 falls to 90%. Sitting him back up settles this.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing, peripheral cyanosis and gouty tophi
steps.find: Warm hands, capillary refill 2 seconds. No clubbing, no peripheral cyanosis, no tophi.

steps.do: Count the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and measure the blood pressure
steps.find: Pulse about 104 to 108/min, irregularly irregular, normal volume. BP 144/86 mmHg.

steps.do: Assess the JVP with him at 45 degrees, then check for hepatojugular reflux
steps.find: JVP raised 5 cm above the sternal angle at 45 degrees. Hepatojugular reflux positive.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the praecordium for the apex beat, heaves and thrills
steps.find: Apex beat displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No heaves or thrills.

steps.do: Auscultate all four areas while he sits up
steps.find: First heart sound varies in intensity, second heart sound normal. No murmurs, no added sounds, no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check the trachea, then assess expansion, percussion and auscultation front and back with him sitting forward (do not lie him flat)
steps.find: Trachea central. Expansion slightly reduced at both bases. Dull to percussion over the lowest few centimetres of both bases, resonant above. Fine inspiratory crackles at both bases, up to about the lower third of each lung. No wheeze, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen with him propped up, feel for the liver edge and check for ascites
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. Liver edge just palpable, smooth and non-tender. No ascites.

steps.do: Press for pitting oedema in both legs and over the sacrum, and examine the calves
steps.find: Symmetrical pitting oedema in both legs up to the mid-shins. Mild sacral oedema. Calves soft and non-tender.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the right first metatarsophalangeal joint, the site of the recent gout flare
steps.find: No redness, warmth or swelling now. The flare has settled.

bedside.find: 92 kg today, compared with his usual of about 88 kg: a gain of about 4 kg.
Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 104 to 108/min, in keeping with his known AF.
About 95% on nasal prongs. He feels a little easier.
6.4 mmol/L (normal).
The nurse has recorded it. The ECG will be given in Part 2 for interpretation.
No blood, protein, leucocytes or nitrites.

amsa-412.key: Bernard has the signs of fluid overload (congestion) in both the lungs and the body: JVP raised 5 cm with positive hepatojugular reflux, fine bibasal crackles with dullness at both bases, pitting oedema to the mid-shins with sacral oedema, a palpable liver and about 4 kg of weight gain. This fits acute decompensated heart failure on a background of cardiomegaly (displaced apex). He is warm and well perfused with a normal BP, so he is congested but not shocked. He is tachypnoeic with SpO2 91% on room air and cannot lie flat, so he needs to stay upright and have oxygen titrated to 92 to 96%. There is no fever, wheeze, murmur, focal chest sign or unilateral calf swelling to suggest pneumonia, asthma, a valve problem or a DVT/PE as an alternative.

amsa-413.vitals: Room air (after the paramedic neb finished): RR 32/min, SpO2 92% on room air, HR 126/min regular, BP 128/76 mmHg, Temp 37.2 °C, alert. On arrival with the salbutamol neb running on O2 8 L/min: RR 34/min, SpO2 98%, HR 130/min regular, BP 130/80 mmHg.
amsa-413.general: A young woman in running clothes, sitting bolt upright and leaning forward with her hands on her knees. She is anxious and in obvious respiratory distress, using her neck (accessory) muscles to breathe. She can speak only 3 or 4 words per breath, and her wheeze can be heard from the end of the bed. She is alert and not exhausted. No central or peripheral cyanosis. Fine tremor of both hands. On the cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place. She cannot lie back: "I can't... I need to sit up."

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and tremor
steps.find: Warm hands, capillary refill under 2 seconds. No clubbing. No peripheral cyanosis. Fine tremor of both hands.

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume; confirm the blood pressure
steps.find: Pulse 126/min, regular, good volume. BP 128/76 mmHg.

steps.do: Inspect the lips, tongue and face for swelling, listen for stridor and a hoarse voice, check the trachea
steps.find: No swelling of the lips, tongue or face. No stridor. Voice normal apart from breathlessness. Trachea central. Using her neck muscles to breathe.

steps.do: Inspect the skin for hives, rash and atopic changes
steps.find: Dry, scaly eczema in both elbow creases. No hives or rash.

steps.do: Inspect the shape of the chest and how it moves, check expansion on both sides, feel for tenderness
steps.find: Chest looks hyperinflated. Expansion reduced but equal on both sides. Chest wall not tender, no bruising.

steps.do: Percuss the front and back of the chest, comparing the two sides
steps.find: Resonant throughout and the same on both sides. No one-sided hyper-resonance or dullness.

steps.do: Listen to the front and back of the chest, comparing the two sides
steps.find: Widespread high-pitched expiratory wheeze over both lungs, with a prolonged expiratory phase. Air entry reduced but present and equal on both sides. Not a silent chest. No crackles, no bronchial breathing, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Listen to the heart
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, tachycardic, no murmurs.

steps.do: Inspect and feel both calves for swelling and tenderness
steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling, both sides the same.

bedside.find: She is too breathless to do a reliable blow at the moment. Do not hold up treatment to get one.
Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 126/min, looks like sinus.

bedside.test: Response to treatment (only if oxygen and salbutamol are ordered)
bedside.find: After a few minutes she can say short sentences, the wheeze is a little quieter, SpO2 about 95% on oxygen, HR stays about 120/min, and her tremor is a bit worse.
Both have been taken and recorded. The results are given in Part 2.

amsa-413.key: This is severe but not life-threatening acute asthma. She speaks only 3 to 4 words per breath, uses her accessory muscles, is in obvious distress and has an SpO2 of 92% on room air. She is still alert and not cyanosed, and her wheeze is audible, so this is not a silent chest. Wheeze and air entry are the same on both sides, percussion is resonant and symmetrical and the trachea is central, which points away from a pneumothorax. There is no angioedema, stridor or hives to suggest anaphylaxis, and her calves are normal, which counts against a DVT or PE (but does not rule out PE, as she takes the combined pill). Her tremor and tachycardia fit the salbutamol and her distress.

amsa-414.vitals: RR 26/min, SpO2 92% on 2 L/min nasal prongs, HR 106/min regular, BP 146/84 mmHg, Temp 37.8 °C, BGL 9.6 mmol/L, alert (AVPU A)
amsa-414.general: An older man sitting bolt upright and leaning forward with his hands on his knees (tripod position). He is breathing out through pursed lips and using his neck and shoulder muscles to breathe. He speaks in short sentences and stops to catch his breath. He is not cyanosed on oxygen. He is alert, answers appropriately and looks frightened but cooperative. He smells of cigarettes. He is on nasal prongs and a cardiac monitor, with an IV cannula in place. He cannot lie flat.

steps.do: Inspect the fingers and nails, feel the temperature, check capillary refill, and test for a flapping tremor with the arms outstretched and wrists extended
steps.find: Heavy tar staining of the right index and middle fingers. No clubbing. Hands warm, capillary refill 2 seconds. No flapping tremor (asterixis).

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and check the blood pressure
steps.find: Pulse 106/min, regular, normal volume. BP 146/84 mmHg.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for central cyanosis, assess the JVP with him sitting upright, check the tracheal position and measure the cricosternal distance
steps.find: No central cyanosis on oxygen. Pursed-lip breathing. JVP not raised, though hard to see because of his neck muscle use. Trachea central. Cricosternal distance reduced to 2 finger-breadths. Tracheal tug present.

steps.do: Inspect the chest from the front, side and back for shape, scars and breathing pattern
steps.find: Barrel-shaped chest with an increased front-to-back diameter. No scars. Accessory muscle use, with a prolonged expiratory phase.

steps.do: Assess chest expansion front and back, and feel for the apex beat
steps.find: Expansion reduced but equal on both sides. Apex beat hard to feel.

steps.do: Percuss the front, sides and back, comparing left with right, including over the area of cardiac dullness
steps.find: Hyper-resonant throughout both sides. Loss of the normal cardiac dullness. No focal dullness.

steps.do: Auscultate the front, sides and back, comparing left with right, ask him to cough and listen again, and test vocal resonance
steps.find: Breath sounds reduced throughout both lungs, with a prolonged expiratory phase. Widespread expiratory polyphonic wheeze on both sides. A few coarse crackles at both bases that change after coughing. No bronchial breathing, no focal crackles, vocal resonance equal on both sides, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Auscultate the four valve areas
steps.find: Heart sounds soft, dual, no murmurs. No third heart sound.

steps.do: Check for pitting oedema at the ankles and sacrum, and examine both calves for swelling and tenderness
steps.find: No ankle or sacral oedema. Calves soft and non-tender with no swelling on either side.

bedside.find: Sinus tachycardia at about 106/min. The registrar has looked at it and says there is nothing acute: no acute ischaemic changes, and no AF today.
9.6 mmol/L (raised; known type 2 diabetes).
92% on 2 L/min nasal prongs, already at the top of his 88 to 92% target.
Yellow purulent sputum. Not green and no blood. Sample can go for microscopy and culture.

amsa-414.key: The barrel chest, reduced cricosternal distance, hyper-resonance on both sides and widespread expiratory wheeze with a prolonged expiratory phase point to COPD with hyperinflation. With his yellow sputum and a temperature of 37.8 °C, this fits an infective exacerbation. The signs are symmetrical, with no bronchial breathing or focal crackles, no raised JVP, no third heart sound, no oedema and soft calves. This argues against pneumonia, pneumothorax, heart failure and DVT. He is tachypnoeic with accessory muscle use and an SpO2 already at the top of his 88 to 92% target, so the oxygen should not be increased. There is no flap or drowsiness, but watch for both because they would suggest rising CO2.

amsa-415.vitals: Latest set at 10:08 on room air, before ED treatment: RR 34/min, SpO2 87%, HR 114/min regular, BP 184/100 mmHg, temp 36.9 °C, alert (A on AVPU), capillary refill 2 s, BGL 11.4 mmol/L (from triage at 10:02). Triage at 10:02 was RR 32, SpO2 88%, HR 108, BP 186/98. With oxygen, SpO2 rises to about 91%. After more GTN, HR comes down to about 104/min and BP to about 170/92 mmHg.
amsa-415.general: He is a 70-year-old man (84 kg) in severe respiratory distress. He is sitting bolt upright on the trolley, leaning forward with his hands on his knees, and is using his neck and shoulder muscles to breathe. He can say only 2 or 3 words at a time. His lips are dusky and he is slightly sweaty. He is frightened but alert and cooperative. There is nicotine staining on his right fingers. There is a healed midline sternotomy scar, a healed transverse scar low on the front of the neck (thyroidectomy) and a healed scar along the inside of the left leg (vein harvest). He is on a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect and feel both hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and test for asterixis.
steps.find: Hands are cool and slightly clammy (vasoconstricted). Capillary refill is 2 seconds. Nicotine staining on the right fingers. No clubbing and no asterixis.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume.
steps.find: Regular, normal volume, 114/min before treatment (about 104/min after GTN). No radio-radial delay.

steps.do: Recheck the BP manually or read it from the monitor.
steps.find: 184/100 mmHg before treatment (about 170/92 mmHg after GTN). He is hypertensive and not shocked.

steps.do: Look at the JVP with him sitting at 90° (he cannot lie back), then test for hepatojugular reflux.
steps.find: JVP is raised, 6 cm above the sternal angle at 90°. Hepatojugular reflux is positive.

steps.do: Inspect the chest, feel for the apex beat and palpate for heaves and thrills.
steps.find: Healed midline sternotomy scar. Apex beat is displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No heaves or thrills.

steps.do: Listen over all 4 valve areas with the bell and diaphragm.
steps.find: First and second heart sounds are present, with an added third heart sound (gallop rhythm). No murmurs and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check the trachea is central and assess chest expansion at the front and back.
steps.find: Trachea is central. Expansion is reduced at both bases and symmetrical.

steps.do: Percuss and listen at the front and back from apices to bases, and test vocal resonance.
steps.find: Both bases are dull to percussion up to about the lower third on each side, resonant above. Breath sounds and vocal resonance are reduced at both bases. Fine inspiratory crackles above the dullness, up to both mid zones. No wheeze and no bronchial breathing. No hyperresonance.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen for the liver edge and check for ascites (shifting dullness).
steps.find: Soft. The liver edge is smooth, mildly tender and 2 cm below the right costal margin. No ascites.

steps.do: Press for pitting oedema in both legs and over the sacrum, compare the calves and feel the foot pulses.
steps.find: Symmetrical pitting oedema in both legs up to the knees, with mild sacral oedema. Calves are soft and non-tender with no difference between them. Healed vein-harvest scar on the inside of the left leg. Foot pulses are present but hard to feel through the oedema.

bedside.find: 11.4 mmol/L at triage. High, in a man with known type 2 diabetes.
Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 108–114/min, consistent with sinus tachycardia. No ectopics or arrhythmia seen.
87–88% on room air, worsening between triage and review. With controlled oxygen it rises to about 91%.
Already recorded by the nurse. The formal 12-lead result is given in Part 2.
Already sent by the nurse. Results are given in Part 2.
84 kg, recorded as a baseline for daily weights during diuresis.

amsa-415.key: The red zone RR and SpO2 are getting worse and the BP is high, so this is hypertensive acute pulmonary oedema. He needs action straight away: keep him upright, give controlled oxygen, call senior help and start nitrates. He has clear signs of congestive heart failure: a raised JVP with positive hepatojugular reflux, a displaced apex with an S3 gallop, fine crackles to the mid zones, a tender enlarged liver, and symmetrical pitting oedema to the knees with sacral oedema. Both bases are dull with reduced breath sounds, which suggests bilateral effusions on top of the oedema. A central trachea, symmetrical findings, no wheeze and soft calves make pneumothorax, a one-sided (possibly malignant) effusion, bronchospasm and DVT/PE less likely.

amsa-416.vitals: 10:10, seated at rest on room air: HR 88 beats/min regular, BP 136/82 mmHg, RR 18 breaths/min, SpO2 94% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C. Weight 72 kg, height 163 cm, BMI 27 kg/m2.
amsa-416.general: Phoebe is alert and comfortable sitting at rest. She speaks in full sentences and has an occasional loose cough. After walking into the room she does mild pursed-lip breathing, which settles once she sits. No accessory muscle use at rest. No cyanosis or pallor. She is overweight (BMI 27). There is no oxygen or inhaler at the bedside.

steps.do: Inspect the hands and nails for clubbing, nicotine staining and peripheral cyanosis. Ask her to hold her hands out with the wrists cocked back to look for a CO2 retention flap and a fine tremor.
steps.find: Nicotine staining of the right index and middle fingers. No clubbing. No peripheral cyanosis. No flap. No fine tremor.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for central cyanosis, and the conjunctivae for pallor.
steps.find: No central cyanosis. Conjunctivae pink, not pale.

steps.do: Check the trachea is midline and look at the JVP with her at 45 degrees. Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes from behind.
steps.find: Trachea midline. JVP not raised. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect the chest from the front, side and back for shape, scars, symmetry and pattern of breathing.
steps.find: The front-to-back diameter is increased (barrel-shaped chest). No scars or deformity. No accessory muscle use or intercostal recession at rest. Mild pursed-lip breathing only after exertion.

steps.do: Assess chest expansion at the front and back.
steps.find: Expansion is reduced but symmetrical on both sides.

steps.do: Percuss the front, sides and back, comparing side to side, and percuss over the area of cardiac dullness.
steps.find: Hyper-resonant throughout both lung fields, with reduced cardiac dullness. No dull areas, and no sign of effusion or consolidation.

steps.do: Auscultate the front, sides and back, comparing side to side, listening to breath sounds and added sounds.
steps.find: Breath sounds reduced throughout, with a prolonged expiratory phase and scattered polyphonic expiratory wheeze on both sides. No crackles, and in particular no fine basal crackles. No bronchial breathing. No pleural rub.

steps.do: Palpate the apex beat and auscultate the four heart areas.
steps.find: Apex beat hard to feel because the chest is hyperinflated. Heart sounds dual with no added sounds or murmur.

steps.do: Check for pitting oedema at the ankles and sacrum, and examine the calves.
steps.find: No ankle or sacral oedema. Calves soft and non-tender.

bedside.find: 8.4 mmol/L. Mildly raised, as expected in known type 2 diabetes. No acute hyperglycaemia.
Negative for glucose, ketones, protein, blood, leucocytes and nitrites.
Small amount of white mucoid sputum. Not purulent and no blood.

amsa-416.key: Phoebe has hyperinflation (barrel chest, hyper-resonance, reduced cardiac dullness) and airflow obstruction (reduced breath sounds, prolonged expiration, expiratory wheeze), with a resting SpO2 of 94% on room air. This fits COPD in a 50 pack-year smoker, which needs to be confirmed on spirometry. The important negatives are no clubbing, fine crackles or lymph nodes (against fibrosis and against obvious lung cancer), no raised JVP or oedema (against heart failure), and no fever or purulent sputum (against an acute flare-up). This means she can be managed in general practice, but she still needs an ECG and cardiovascular risk assessment because she has diabetes and smokes.

amsa-417.vitals: Temperature 36.7 °C, HR 76 bpm regular, BP 116/72 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air; weight 58 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 21 kg/m²
amsa-417.general: Well-looking young woman sitting comfortably and talking in full sentences. Not pale or jaundiced. Not dehydrated, and she looks well nourished (BMI 21). No signs of systemic illness. A little anxious and embarrassed but appropriate.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for clubbing, koilonychia, leuconychia and palmar pallor or erythema
steps.find: No clubbing, koilonychia or leuconychia. No palmar pallor. Normal.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae for pallor and the sclerae for icterus, episcleritis or redness
steps.find: Conjunctivae pink. No scleral icterus. No episcleritis or red eye.

steps.do: Inspect the lips, tongue and oral mucosa for ulcers, angular stomatitis and glossitis
steps.find: No mouth ulcers, angular stomatitis or glossitis. Mucous membranes moist.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular nodes, including the left supraclavicular fossa (Virchow's node)
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect the shins for erythema nodosum and the elbows, knees and buttocks for an itchy blistering rash (dermatitis herpetiformis); examine the large joints for swelling or tenderness
steps.find: No rash, no erythema nodosum, no dermatitis herpetiformis. Joints normal, with no swelling, tenderness or reduced movement.

steps.do: Lie her flat, expose the abdomen and inspect for distension, scars, visible masses or peristalsis
steps.find: Mildly distended. No scars, visible masses or visible peristalsis. Moves normally with breathing.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all nine regions, watching her face, checking for guarding, rebound and masses (especially the right iliac fossa), then feel for the liver, spleen and kidneys
steps.find: Soft. Mild tenderness across the lower abdomen (left and right iliac fossae), with no guarding or rebound. No masses, including in the right iliac fossa. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Kidneys not ballotable.

steps.do: Percuss for tympany, liver span and shifting dullness; listen for bowel sounds and bruits
steps.find: Tympanic throughout. Normal liver span. No shifting dullness. Normal bowel sounds. No bruits.

steps.do: Offer with consent and a chaperone; inspect for skin tags, fissures and fistulae, then do a digital rectal examination
steps.find: No perianal skin tags, fissures or fistulae. No tenderness or mass on rectal examination. Soft brown stool on the glove, with no blood or mucus.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lungs
steps.find: Heart sounds dual with no murmurs. Chest clear with equal air entry on both sides. Normal.

bedside.find: Normal. Negative for blood, leucocytes, nitrites, protein, glucose and ketones.
Negative.

amsa-417.key: Jessica is well. Her observations are normal, she is afebrile and her BMI is steady at 21. She has no pallor, clubbing, jaundice, mouth ulcers, lymph nodes, rash or joint signs, so there is nothing to suggest anaemia, malabsorption, IBD or cancer. The only abdominal findings are mild distension and mild lower abdominal tenderness, with no guarding and no masses (including the right iliac fossa). The rectal examination is normal with no blood, and the bedside tests exclude a urinary cause and pregnancy. Finding no alarm signs, together with her history, supports a working diagnosis of IBS, to be confirmed with the first-line blood and stool tests.

amsa-418.vitals: Temp 38.6 °C, HR 104 beats/min regular, BP 128/76 mmHg, RR 22/min, SpO2 94% on room air (10:15). Weight 82 kg.
amsa-418.general: Looks unwell, flushed and warm to touch. Coughs often and is mildly short of breath at rest, but speaks in full sentences. Winces and holds the right side of his chest when he breathes in deeply. Not cyanosed. Alert and fully oriented, Abbreviated Mental Test 10/10.

steps.do: Inspect the sputum for colour, volume, smell and blood
steps.find: About a teaspoon of thick yellow-green sputum with an offensive smell. No blood, not pink or frothy.

steps.do: Check the mucous membranes and capillary refill
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes. Capillary refill 2 seconds.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands for temperature, clubbing, peripheral cyanosis and asterixis
steps.find: Warm hands. No clubbing, no peripheral cyanosis, no flap.

steps.do: Examine the throat, palpate the cervical lymph nodes, check the trachea position and the JVP
steps.find: Throat normal. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Trachea midline. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect the chest wall and assess chest expansion, front and back
steps.find: No scars or deformity. Expansion reduced at the right base, normal elsewhere.

steps.do: Percuss front and back, comparing sides
steps.find: Dull over the right lower zone posteriorly. Resonant elsewhere.

steps.do: Auscultate front and back, comparing sides, and test vocal resonance
steps.find: Bronchial breath sounds with coarse crackles and increased vocal resonance over the right lower zone posteriorly. Left lung clear. No wheeze, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and look for ankle and sacral oedema
steps.find: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs or added sounds. No ankle or sacral oedema.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both calves for swelling, tenderness, redness and warmth, and compare calf size
steps.find: Both calves soft and non-tender, the same size, with no swelling, redness or warmth.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the abdomen
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. A few small fading bruises from the injections. Well-healed appendicectomy scar.

bedside.find: Sinus tachycardia 104/min, normal axis, normal intervals, no ST-segment or T-wave changes. No acute ischaemic change.
10/10. Not confused.

amsa-418.key: The signs of consolidation at the right lower zone (reduced expansion, dullness, bronchial breathing, coarse crackles and increased vocal resonance), together with fever, tachycardia, tachypnoea, SpO2 94% and offensive purulent sputum, point to right lower lobe bacterial pneumonia starting soon after his hospital discharge. Normal calves, a JVP that is not raised, no oedema and an ECG without ischaemic change make PE, heart failure and ACS less likely, although they do not exclude them. He is alert and his BP is normal, but he is dehydrated and his oxygen level is borderline, so his severity needs scoring and his observations need repeating.

amsa-420.vitals: Temp 36.7 °C, HR 76 bpm regular, BP 122/76 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, alert, pain 2/10, weight 68 kg
amsa-420.general: Comfortable at rest, alert and talking in full sentences. A little embarrassed but cooperative. Not pale, not jaundiced, not distressed. Moves easily on and off the couch.

steps.do: Look for pallor in the conjunctivae and palmar creases, check mucous membranes, capillary refill and skin turgor
steps.find: No conjunctival or palmar pallor. No koilonychia. Mucous membranes moist, capillary refill under 2 seconds, normal skin turgor: well hydrated.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the thyroid and the cervical and supraclavicular nodes
steps.find: No goitre. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy (Virchow's node not palpable).

steps.do: Expose the abdomen and inspect for distension, visible peristalsis and the four port-site wounds
steps.find: Mildly distended. No visible peristalsis. Four laparoscopic port-site wounds (umbilical, epigastric and two right upper quadrant) are healing, clean and dry, with no redness, swelling or discharge.

steps.do: Palpate all nine regions lightly then deeply, watching her face, and check for liver, spleen and bladder
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, with no guarding or rebound. An indentable, non-tender tubular mass in the left iliac fossa, consistent with faecal loading. No other masses. No hepatosplenomegaly. Bladder not palpable.

steps.do: Palpate each port site and both groins, and ask her to cough
steps.find: No hernia at any port site or in either groin, including on coughing. Umbilical port site only mildly sore to touch.

steps.do: Percuss for tympany and shifting dullness, then listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Mildly tympanic, with no shifting dullness. Bowel sounds present and normal, not tinkling and not absent.

steps.do: With consent and a chaperone, in the left lateral position, part the buttocks gently and inspect the anal margin
steps.find: A small superficial split in the posterior midline of the anal margin, consistent with an acute anal fissure. No sentinel skin tag. No external haemorrhoids. No perianal abscess.

steps.do: With consent, a chaperone and plenty of lubricant, do a gentle DRE
steps.find: Uncomfortable for her. Normal anal tone. Rectum loaded with hard stool. No rectal mass. A trace of bright red blood on the glove, with no melaena.

steps.do: Palpate the spine, then test power, sensation and reflexes in the legs and check perianal sensation
steps.find: No spinal tenderness. Normal power, sensation and reflexes in both legs. Normal perianal sensation.

bedside.find: Normal: no blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites, glucose or ketones
Negative
