amsa-420.key: Normal observations, a soft non-tender abdomen, flatus and normal (not tinkling) bowel sounds argue strongly against postoperative ileus, adhesive obstruction or a surgical complication. Faecal loading in the left iliac fossa and hard stool in the rectum confirm constipation. The posterior midline fissure explains the bright red blood on wiping. There is no rectal mass, no pallor and no neurological deficit, so this fits opioid-induced (and iron-associated) constipation with an acute anal fissure.

amsa-436.vitals: Triage 14:30 on room air: RR 18/min, SpO2 96%, BP 108/64 mmHg, HR 112 bpm regular, temperature 38.6 °C, alert (AVPU A), pain 5/10, CRT 2 seconds, BGL 5.8 mmol/L, weight 75 kg
amsa-436.general: Jaundiced, flushed and mildly uncomfortable on the trolley. He looks shivery and scratches his arms now and then. Alert, oriented and speaking in full sentences. His arms and shoulders are thin and his abdomen is large. Partway through, the nurse reports a rigor: "He's just had a really bad shivering episode, he was shaking all over."

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms, check the peripheral temperature and capillary refill, look at the forearm skin, look for a tremor with the hands held out, and test for asterixis with the wrists cocked back
steps.find: Palmar erythema and leukonychia, no clubbing. Excoriations on both forearms and several bruises on the forearms. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. No asterixis. Warm peripheries, CRT 2 seconds.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae, mucous membranes and parotids, and assess the JVP
steps.find: Scleral icterus. Dry mucous membranes. No parotid enlargement. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect the upper chest and breasts, auscultate the heart, then percuss and auscultate the lung bases
steps.find: 5 spider naevi on the upper chest and mild gynaecomastia. Dual heart sounds, no murmurs. Chest clear with no dullness at the bases (no pleural effusion or basal consolidation).

steps.do: Inspect the exposed abdomen with the patient lying flat
steps.find: Distended with bulging flanks and an everted umbilicus. No scars. No caput medusae.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all regions, looking for guarding, rigidity and rebound tenderness, then palpate for the liver and spleen
steps.find: Mild tenderness all over the abdomen. No guarding, rigidity or rebound tenderness. Liver not palpable. Spleen tip palpable on deep inspiration. No masses.

steps.do: Percuss from the midline out to the flanks, then test for shifting dullness
steps.find: Dull in both flanks with shifting dullness present, consistent with ascites. Not tympanic.

steps.do: Auscultate for bowel sounds and examine the hernial orifices
steps.find: Bowel sounds present and normal. No hernias.

steps.do: Digital rectal examination with consent and a chaperone, looking for melaena or blood
steps.find: Brown stool, no melaena, no fresh blood, no mass.

steps.do: Inspect the legs and press over the shins and ankles for pitting oedema
steps.find: Pitting oedema to the ankles on both sides.

steps.do: Check orientation and attention (months of the year backwards)
steps.find: Oriented to time, place and person. Says the months backwards without error. No clinical sign of hepatic encephalopathy.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L
Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, normal axis, normal intervals, no acute ischaemic changes
Dark amber urine. Bilirubin positive. Leucocytes, nitrites and blood negative. No sign of a urinary source

amsa-436.key: Roger has a fever of 38.6 °C, a heart rate of 112 and a borderline BP, followed by a rigor. With known cirrhosis this points to sepsis, so he needs blood cultures and a senior review straight away. He has many stigmata of chronic liver disease, jaundice, splenomegaly and ascites confirmed by shifting dullness. Together with mild diffuse tenderness and no peritonism, this fits spontaneous bacterial peritonitis rather than a surgical abdomen and calls for a diagnostic tap. There is no asterixis, his attention is intact and there is no melaena, so encephalopathy and GI bleeding are unlikely. The fine tremor about 17 hours after his last drink raises the risk of early alcohol withdrawal.

amsa-438.vitals: HR 84 bpm regular, BP 118/72 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.8 °C. Weight 64 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 20.2 kg/m2 (down from 70 kg 6 months ago).
amsa-438.general: Thin young man sitting comfortably, chatting easily but a bit anxious. He looks mildly pale. He is alert and well hydrated, not jaundiced and in no distress. There is no cachexia or muscle wasting beyond his slim build.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for clubbing, koilonychia, leukonychia and palmar pallor. Feel the radial pulse.
steps.find: No clubbing, koilonychia or leukonychia. Mild palmar crease pallor. Radial pulse 84 and regular.

steps.do: Pull down the lower eyelid to look for conjunctival pallor. Look for scleral icterus and for red eyes (episcleritis, uveitis).
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. No scleral icterus. Eyes are white and not inflamed.

steps.do: Inspect the oral mucosa, lips, tongue and gums with a pen torch.
steps.find: Two small, shallow aphthous ulcers, one on the inner lower lip and one on the buccal mucosa. No angular stomatitis or glossitis. Gums are normal.

steps.do: Assess mouth opening, dentition, Mallampati class and neck movement.
steps.find: Good mouth opening (more than 3 finger-breadths). Full natural dentition with no loose teeth, caps or dentures. Mallampati class I. Full neck flexion and extension.

steps.do: Inspect the shins and skin for erythema nodosum and pyoderma gangrenosum. Look at the large joints for swelling.
steps.find: No erythema nodosum, pyoderma or rash. No joint swelling, effusion or tenderness.

steps.do: Auscultate the praecordium and both lung fields.
steps.find: Heart sounds dual with no murmurs. Chest clear with equal air entry on both sides.

steps.do: Lie him flat. Inspect, then palpate lightly and then deeply in all regions, asking about tenderness. Check for guarding, rebound, masses and hepatosplenomegaly.
steps.find: Not distended and no scars. Soft, with mild tenderness in the right iliac fossa. No guarding or rebound. No palpable mass in the right iliac fossa or elsewhere. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.

steps.area: Abdomen: percussion, auscultation and hernial orifices
steps.do: Percuss for shifting dullness and tympany. Listen for bowel sounds. Examine the hernial orifices.
steps.find: Resonant to percussion with no shifting dullness. Bowel sounds normal (not tinkling or absent). Hernial orifices clear.

steps.area: Perianal inspection (with consent and a chaperone)
steps.do: Place him in the left lateral position and inspect the perianal skin for tags, fissures, fistula openings and abscess.
steps.find: One small, soft, non-tender perianal skin tag. No fistula opening, abscess, fissure or induration.

steps.do: Offer a digital rectal examination.
steps.find: Deferred. It will be done at the start of the colonoscopy under sedation.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L (normal, non-fasting).
Normal: no blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites, glucose or ketones. Specific gravity 1.015.
Sinus rhythm at 84 bpm with a normal axis and normal intervals. No ischaemic changes.

bedside.test: Pre-admission bloods (FBC, iron studies, CRP, UEC, LFTs, coeliac serology)
bedside.find: Collected today. The results will be available in Part 2.

amsa-438.key: The important findings are a 6 kg weight loss (BMI now 20.2), mild pallor that fits his known iron deficiency, aphthous mouth ulcers, mild right iliac fossa tenderness with no mass and a perianal skin tag. Together they point to ileocolonic Crohn's disease. His observations are normal, he is afebrile, and his abdomen is soft with normal bowel sounds and no distension, guarding or rebound. So there is no sign of a severe flare, obstruction or perforation that would make colonoscopy unsafe now. His airway is normal (Mallampati class I, good mouth opening, no loose teeth) and his heart and chest are normal, so he is fit for day-procedure sedation.

amsa-475.vitals: RR 28/min, SpO2 92% on room air, HR 108/min regular, BP 144/84 mmHg, Temp 36.7 °C, pain 0/10, alert (repeat set after she slid down the trolley; at triage RR 26, SpO2 93% RA, HR 104, BP 148/86)
amsa-475.general: Sitting upright and propped on pillows. Mildly breathless at rest. Speaks in sentences but stops now and then for breath. Not cyanosed, pale or sweaty. Overweight (84 kg). On a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place. Worried and asks whether this is her heart. If you lie her flat she becomes more breathless and asks to sit up again.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands: temperature, capillary refill, clubbing, tar staining, tremor, peripheral cyanosis
steps.find: Warm peripheries, capillary refill 2 seconds. No clubbing, no tar staining, no tremor, no peripheral cyanosis.

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume; take the blood pressure
steps.find: Pulse 108/min, regular, normal volume. BP 144/84 mmHg.

steps.do: With her at 45°, measure the JVP height above the sternal angle, then press over the liver to test hepatojugular reflux; check for goitre and lymph nodes
steps.find: JVP raised, 5 cm above the sternal angle at 45°. Hepatojugular reflux positive. No goitre, no cervical lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect the chest, find the apex beat, and feel for heaves and thrills
steps.find: Apex beat displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No parasternal heave, no thrills.

steps.do: Listen at all four areas with the bell and diaphragm, with manoeuvres for murmurs
steps.find: Dual heart sounds plus a third heart sound (gallop rhythm). No murmurs. No pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check tracheal position and chest expansion, percuss, and listen to the front and back of the chest with her sitting forward
steps.find: Trachea central. Expansion equal on both sides. Dull to percussion at both bases. Fine inspiratory crackles at both bases up to the lower third of the chest, with reduced breath sounds at the bases. No wheeze, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness and the liver edge, and check for ascites (shifting dullness)
steps.find: Soft, non-tender. Smooth, non-tender liver edge 2 cm below the right costal margin. No ascites.

steps.do: Press for pitting oedema in the legs and over the sacrum, and examine the calves for DVT
steps.find: Pitting oedema in both legs up to the mid-shins, the same on each side. Mild sacral oedema. Calves soft and non-tender.

bedside.find: Regular narrow-complex rhythm, sinus tachycardia at about 108/min, no ectopics or runs
The nurse recorded it at 13:50. The examiner will give you the tracing in Part 2.
9.4 mmol/L
Trace protein. Negative for glucose, blood, leucocytes, nitrites and ketones.
84 kg (record as the baseline for daily weights)

amsa-475.key: She has signs of congestion on both sides of the heart. On the left: bibasal crackles, dull bases from effusions, a displaced apex and an S3. On the right: a JVP raised to 5 cm with positive hepatojugular reflux, pitting oedema to the mid-shins, sacral oedema and a smooth hepatomegaly. A year after an anterior STEMI, this points to decompensated biventricular heart failure. She is tachypnoeic with borderline oxygen saturations that get worse lying back, but she is warm, normotensive and afebrile with no murmur, wheeze or bronchial breathing. So she is not in shock, and valve disease, COPD and pneumonia are less likely. She needs to sit upright, have oxygen titrated to SpO2 92 to 96% and get IV diuretic now.

amsa-476.vitals: HR 108 bpm regular, BP 118/74 mmHg lying, RR 18 /min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, capillary refill 3 seconds centrally, BGL 6.2 mmol/L, alert (AVPU A), pain 5/10
amsa-476.general: Pale, slightly clammy and anxious, lying in an acute bay with monitoring attached. Peripheries cool, capillary refill 3 seconds centrally. Alert and oriented to time, place and person, answering clearly. Slightly yellow sclerae. Thin arms with a visibly swollen abdomen.

steps.do: Feel the peripheries, check central capillary refill, pulse rate and rhythm, and the lying BP. Then check a sitting BP with the patient's safety in mind
steps.find: Cool peripheries, capillary refill 3 seconds centrally, HR 108 regular, BP 118/74 lying. Sitting up: BP 100/64 and HR 124, and he feels light-headed. This settles when he lies back.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms, look for clubbing and Dupuytren contracture, inspect the forearms, test for a tremor with the hands held out, and test for asterixis
steps.find: Palmar erythema on both hands, white nails (leukonychia), no clubbing, no Dupuytren contracture. Several bruises on both forearms. Thin arms. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. No asterixis.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae and conjunctivae, feel for parotid enlargement, assess the JVP
steps.find: Scleral icterus. Conjunctival pallor. No parotid enlargement. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect the chest wall for spider naevi and gynaecomastia, listen to the heart and lungs
steps.find: 6 spider naevi over the upper chest and shoulders. Bilateral gynaecomastia. Heart sounds dual with no murmurs. Chest clear with good air entry on both sides.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen lying flat with it fully exposed
steps.find: Distended abdomen with full flanks. No caput medusae. No scars.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all regions, check for Murphy's sign, palpate for the liver and spleen
steps.find: Mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant with no guarding or rebound. Murphy's sign negative. Firm, irregular liver edge 3 cm below the right costal margin. Spleen tip palpable on deep inspiration. No other masses.

steps.do: Percuss out to the flanks, test for shifting dullness, listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Dull to percussion in both flanks, with shifting dullness present (ascites). Bowel sounds normal.

steps.do: Digital rectal examination, with consent and a chaperone
steps.find: Black, tarry stool on the glove (melaena). No fresh blood. No mass.

steps.do: Inspect the legs and press over the shins and ankles to test for pitting oedema
steps.find: Pitting oedema to mid-shin in both legs.

steps.do: Check orientation and attention (months of the year backwards), conscious level, and look for signs of withdrawal
steps.find: Oriented to time, place and person. Says the months backwards without error. Not drowsy. No asterixis. Fine tremor only. Not hallucinating and not agitated.

bedside.find: 6.2 mmol/L
Lying 118/74 mmHg with HR 108. Sitting 100/64 mmHg with HR 124, and he feels light-headed. Settles when he lies back.
Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm, normal axis, normal intervals, no ischaemic ST or T wave changes.

bedside.test: Blood tests, venous gas and ultrasound
bedside.find: Sent. The results will be given in Part 2.

amsa-476.key: James has an active upper GI bleed (haematemesis and melaena on rectal examination). His resting tachycardia, cool peripheries, slow capillary refill and fall in BP on sitting up show significant blood loss, even though his lying BP looks normal. Palmar erythema, leukonychia, bruising, icterus, spider naevi, gynaecomastia and wasted arms, together with a firm irregular liver, a palpable spleen, shifting dullness and leg oedema, point to decompensated cirrhosis with portal hypertension, so the bleed should be treated as variceal. He has no asterixis and his attention is intact, so there is no overt encephalopathy now, but the fine tremor 10 hours after his last drink may be early alcohol withdrawal.

amsa-477.vitals: BP 142/86 mmHg sitting, 138/84 mmHg after 3 minutes standing (no postural drop), HR 74/min regular, RR 14/min, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 36.6 °C, weight 96 kg, height 176 cm, BMI 31 kg/m²
amsa-477.general: Overweight man sitting comfortably, alert and friendly, talking in full sentences. He walks into the room without an aid. He is wearing worn, thin-soled slip-on shoes. No pallor, jaundice or obvious distress.

steps.area: Feet: inspection with shoes and socks off
steps.do: Removes his shoes and socks and inspects both feet, including the soles and between the toes, looking at the skin, callus, ulcers, fissures, infection, deformity or Charcot changes, nails and footwear.
steps.find: Dry skin on both feet, with mild callus under the first metatarsal heads on both sides. No ulcers, fissures or signs of infection. No deformity and no midfoot collapse. The feet are not hot or swollen. Nails normal. His shoes are worn, thin-soled slip-ons with poor support.

steps.do: Feels foot temperature, checks capillary refill, looks at hair distribution, and palpates the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both sides.
steps.find: Feet warm with normal hair. Capillary refill under 2 seconds. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses palpable and equal on both sides.

steps.do: Tests with a 10 g monofilament at the plantar forefoot sites, then a 128 Hz tuning fork from the great toe upwards (medial malleolus, then knee) on both sides.
steps.find: Monofilament not felt at the plantar forefoot sites on either foot. Vibration absent at both great toes, reduced at both medial malleoli and normal at both knees.

steps.do: Tests joint position sense at the great toe, then the ankle. Maps pinprick from distal to proximal on both legs, comparing the two sides, and looks for a sensory level on the trunk.
steps.find: Joint position sense impaired at both great toes and normal at the ankles. Pinprick reduced symmetrically from the toes to mid-shin on both sides, in a stocking distribution. No sensory level on the trunk.

steps.area: Lower limbs: inspection, tone and power
steps.do: Inspects for wasting and fasciculation, checks tone at hip, knee and ankle, and tests power in all muscle groups, including great toe extension.
steps.find: No wasting or fasciculation. Tone normal. Mild weakness of great toe extension on both sides (MRC 4+/5); power otherwise 5/5 throughout.

steps.area: Lower limbs: reflexes, plantars and clonus
steps.do: Tests knee and ankle reflexes (with reinforcement if absent), plantar responses and ankle clonus.
steps.find: Ankle reflexes absent on both sides, even with reinforcement. Knee reflexes present, normal (not brisk) and equal. Plantar responses flexor on both sides. No clonus.

steps.do: Screens sensation (including vibration and pinprick in the hands), power and reflexes in both arms to look for glove involvement or a more widespread process.
steps.find: Sensation, power and reflexes in the upper limbs are normal on both sides.

steps.do: Watches normal gait and heel-to-toe (tandem) walking, then performs Romberg's test, standing close by to steady him.
steps.find: Gait slightly broad-based. Unsteady on tandem walking. Romberg test positive: steady with eyes open, sways and has to step with eyes closed.

steps.do: Inspects and palpates the spine and performs a straight leg raise on both sides.
steps.find: No spinal tenderness or deformity. Straight leg raise negative on both sides.

bedside.find: 11.2 mmol/L (random), above target
142/86 mmHg sitting, 138/84 mmHg after 3 minutes standing. No postural drop and no symptoms on standing.
Glucose trace. Protein negative. Ketones, blood, leucocytes and nitrites negative. (A dipstick will not pick up mild albuminuria, so a urine ACR is needed.)

amsa-477.key: Patrick has symmetrical, length-dependent sensory loss: no monofilament sensation, vibration absent at the toes, joint position sense impaired at the toes and stocking pinprick loss to mid-shin. He also has absent ankle reflexes, mild distal weakness and a positive Romberg test. This fits a diabetic distal symmetrical sensorimotor polyneuropathy with sensory ataxia, which explains why he is unsteady in the dark. Flexor plantars, knee reflexes that are not brisk, no clonus, no sensory level, normal arms and a normal back exam make a cord, cauda equina or central cause unlikely. Palpable pulses rule out peripheral arterial disease. Loss of protective sensation with callus under the metatarsal heads, worn shoes and walking barefoot puts his feet at risk, and the falls risk matters for his main worry.

amsa-576.vitals: HR 98 beats/min regular, BP 126/78 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 38.3 °C, alert (10:10, seated at rest)
amsa-576.general: A tired, flushed young man. He is sitting comfortably and speaking in full sentences, with short bursts of dry cough during the consultation. He is not distressed, not cyanosed and has no increased work of breathing. He looks unwell but not toxic. Weight 82 kg if asked.

steps.do: Inspect the hands for clubbing, nicotine staining and cyanosis, and feel the peripheral temperature
steps.find: Mild nicotine staining of the right index and middle fingers. No clubbing. No peripheral cyanosis. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate and rhythm
steps.find: 98 beats/min, regular, normal volume (high-normal, in keeping with fever).

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes and check capillary refill
steps.find: Mucous membranes moist. Capillary refill under 2 seconds. Clinically well hydrated.

steps.do: Use the otoscope to examine both ear canals and eardrums
steps.find: Ear canals and eardrums normal on both sides.

steps.do: Inspect the nasal mucosa and the oropharynx with a torch and tongue depressor
steps.find: Nasal mucosa swollen and congested with no discharge. Pharynx red. Tonsils not enlarged, with no exudate.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical lymph nodes, check tracheal position and check for neck stiffness
steps.find: No cervical lymphadenopathy. Trachea midline. Neck supple with no meningism.

steps.do: Inspect for work of breathing and chest shape, and assess expansion front and back
steps.find: No accessory muscle use. Normal chest shape. Expansion symmetrical.

steps.do: Percuss front, back and axillae, comparing sides
steps.find: Resonant throughout, symmetrically.

steps.do: Auscultate breath sounds front, back and axillae, comparing sides, and check vocal resonance if indicated
steps.find: Vesicular breath sounds throughout. No crackles, wheeze or bronchial breathing. No pleural rub. Chest clear.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart, check for peripheral oedema and inspect the skin for a rash
steps.find: Heart sounds dual with no murmur. No peripheral oedema. No rash.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L (normal).
Best of 3 is 560 L/min, about 90% of predicted for his age and height (normal; no evidence of airflow obstruction).
No protein, blood, leucocytes, nitrites or glucose. Ketones negative. Specific gravity 1.020 (normal).
Collected at 10:30 and sent to the laboratory. The result is given in Part 2.

amsa-576.key: Charlie has a fever of 38.3 °C, a high-normal heart rate, a red pharynx and a congested nose. His RR, SpO2 (97% on room air) and BP are normal and his chest is clear, with no crackles, bronchial breathing or wheeze. This fits an uncomplicated viral influenza-like illness with no sign of pneumonia, hypoxia, sepsis or an asthma flare. He is well hydrated and has no meningism or rash, so he can be managed at home while the PCR swab is pending, and the swab will answer his COVID question.

amsa-578.vitals: HR 124/min regular, BP 96/58 mmHg lying, RR 20/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 37.9 °C, capillary BGL 13.4 mmol/L, pain 6/10, weight 72 kg
amsa-578.general: Pale and uncomfortable, lying curled on her side, shifting with each wave of cramp, on the trolley with a vomit bowl beside her. Alert and oriented, speaking in full sentences, not confused. Looks dry and tired. No jaundice and no respiratory distress.

steps.do: Feel the temperature of her hands, check capillary refill, and feel the radial pulse for rate and rhythm
steps.find: Cool hands, CRT 3 seconds. Radial pulse 124/min, regular, low volume. No AF.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes and tongue, test skin turgor, and look at the JVP with her lying flat
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes and tongue, reduced skin turgor, JVP not visible lying flat. Clinically at least moderately dehydrated.

steps.area: Postural blood pressure (only if asked, with assistance)
steps.do: Compare the lying BP and HR with the values after sitting her up carefully, with the nurse helping
steps.find: Lying 96/58 with HR 124. Sitting up 76/48 with HR 138; she feels dizzy and lightheaded and is too dizzy to stand. The dizziness eases once she is laid flat again. The sitting SBP of 76 is a red zone value.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart
steps.find: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Rhythm regular.

steps.do: Auscultate the chest
steps.find: Normal breath sounds throughout, no added sounds. Chest clear.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen with her lying flat and exposed
steps.find: Not distended, no scars, no visible masses or pulsations.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all regions, watching her face. Check for guarding and rebound, test Murphy's sign, feel for organomegaly and for a pulsatile aortic mass
steps.find: Soft, with mild diffuse tenderness and no guarding or rebound. No localised tenderness in the RIF, LIF or RUQ; Murphy's sign negative. No masses, no hepatosplenomegaly, no pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Percuss the abdomen and listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Percussion normal, no shifting dullness. Bowel sounds hyperactive.

steps.do: Examine the inguinal and femoral hernial orifices and press on the renal angles
steps.find: Hernial orifices clear. Renal angles not tender.

steps.area: Rectal examination (if offered, with a chaperone and consent)
steps.do: Digital rectal examination, then inspect the glove
steps.find: Liquid brown stool on the glove. No blood or melaena, no masses.

bedside.find: 13.4 mmol/L (hyperglycaemia in known type 2 diabetes)
0.3 mmol/L, normal
No sample yet. She has passed only a little dark urine since this morning; ask the nurse to collect one and start a fluid balance chart
Regular narrow complex tachycardia about 124/min. A 12-lead ECG, bloods and a venous gas are taken by the nurse now; results are given in Part 2

amsa-578.key: Lying flat she is already tachycardic (HR 124) and relatively hypotensive (96/58 against her usual 140/80), with cool hands, a CRT of 3 seconds, dry mucous membranes and little dark urine. That is significant hypovolaemia. If a postural BP is taken, the sitting SBP of 76 is a red zone value: lie her flat, escalate at once and give an IV crystalloid bolus. Her abdomen is soft, with only mild diffuse tenderness, no peritonism or localising signs and hyperactive bowel sounds, and her pulse is regular. This fits gastroenteritis, although it does not exclude early mesenteric ischaemia in a 69-year-old with vascular risk factors.

amsa-582.vitals: RR 29/min, SpO2 92% on room air, HR 110/min regular, BP 144/84 mmHg, Temp 37.6 °C, alert (AVPU A), CRT 2 s (repeat set at 10:55; at triage 10:40: RR 27, SpO2 92% RA, HR 104, BP 148/86, Temp 37.6 °C)
amsa-582.general: Thin, cachectic man (62 kg) with temporal wasting, sitting bolt upright on the trolley and visibly anxious. He is using his neck muscles to breathe and speaks in short sentences, pausing for breath. His voice is hoarse. He is not cyanosed and not drowsy. He is on a monitor with an IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and fingers, look for clubbing (Schamroth's window), check for asterixis, and feel temperature and capillary refill
steps.find: Finger clubbing with loss of the Schamroth window. Heavy nicotine staining. No asterixis. Hands warm, capillary refill 2 seconds.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for central cyanosis and the conjunctivae for pallor; note the voice
steps.find: No central cyanosis. Temporal wasting. Hoarse voice. Otherwise normal.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular nodes from behind, and assess the JVP at 45 degrees
steps.find: A hard, non-tender 1.5 cm lymph node in the right supraclavicular fossa. No other nodes palpable. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Palpate the trachea in the suprasternal notch
steps.find: Trachea deviated to the left.

steps.do: Inspect the chest wall and assess chest expansion front and back
steps.find: Accessory muscle use. Expansion reduced on the right; normal on the left. No scars or chest wall deformity.

steps.do: Percuss both sides from the apices to the bases, anteriorly and posteriorly, comparing side to side
steps.find: Stony dull on the right from about the 2nd intercostal space anteriorly (mid-scapula posteriorly) down to the base. Left side resonant throughout.

steps.do: Auscultate breath sounds and test vocal resonance on both sides, front and back
steps.find: Right: breath sounds absent and vocal resonance reduced over the dull area, with bronchial breathing just above the upper level of dullness. Left: vesicular breath sounds with a prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze or crackles, normal vocal resonance.

steps.do: Palpate the apex and auscultate the praecordium
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs and no added sounds.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness and hepatomegaly, and check for ascites
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No hepatomegaly and no ascites.

steps.do: Check for pitting oedema and examine the calves
steps.find: No peripheral oedema. Calves soft and non-tender.

bedside.find: 8.9 mmol/L (known type 2 diabetes)
Small amount of white sputum with streaks of blood
Recorded by the nurse at 10:45; the full ECG is given with the results in Part 2

bedside.test: Chest X-ray, bloods and venous gas
bedside.find: Requested and sent; the results are given in Part 2

amsa-582.key: He has a large right pleural effusion: the trachea is pushed to the left, expansion is reduced on the right, and the right side is stony dull up to the 2nd intercostal space with absent breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance. COPD does not cause finger clubbing, so the clubbing, the hard right supraclavicular node, the cachexia and the hoarse voice in a 50 pack-year smoker point strongly to lung cancer causing a malignant effusion. He has no signs of heart failure (JVP not raised, normal heart sounds, no oedema, no hepatomegaly or ascites), which makes a transudate unlikely. His SpO2 of 92% on room air is within his COPD target of 88 to 92%.

amsa-583.vitals: RR 28/min, SpO2 92% on room air, HR 116/min regular, BP 132/80 mmHg, Temp 36.8 °C, alert (AVPU A). At triage 15 minutes earlier: RR 26, SpO2 93% RA, HR 112, BP 134/82.
amsa-583.general: Sitting bolt upright, leaning forward with his hands on his knees, anxious and distressed. Speaks only 3 or 4 words per breath. Audible expiratory wheeze from the end of the bed. Using his neck (sternocleidomastoid) muscles to breathe, with a tracheal tug. Alert and responding properly, not drowsy or exhausted. Not cyanosed. No rash or flushing that you can see. Weight about 78 kg. Cannula in, on a cardiac monitor. He cannot lie flat.

steps.area: Skin, face and upper airway (anaphylaxis screen)
steps.do: Inspect the skin for urticaria and flushing, look at the lips, tongue and face for swelling, and listen for stridor and any change in voice
steps.find: No urticaria or flushing. No angioedema of the lips, tongue or face. No stridor. Voice normal apart from the breathlessness.

steps.do: Check temperature, capillary refill, clubbing, tremor and peripheral cyanosis
steps.find: Warm hands, capillary refill 2 seconds. No clubbing. No peripheral cyanosis. Fine tremor (after his Ventolin).

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume and confirm the BP
steps.find: Pulse 116/min, regular, good volume. BP 132/80.

steps.do: Look for central cyanosis, examine the nasal mucosa and check the JVP
steps.find: No central cyanosis of the tongue or lips. Nasal mucosa pale and swollen, fitting allergic rhinitis. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Palpate the trachea for position and look for tracheal tug
steps.find: Trachea central. Tracheal tug present.

steps.do: Inspect the shape and movement of the chest and look for scars, then check expansion on both sides and feel for surgical emphysema
steps.find: Hyperexpanded chest, no scars, wounds or deformity. Expansion reduced but equal on both sides. No surgical emphysema.

steps.do: Percuss the front, sides and back, comparing left with right
steps.find: Resonant throughout, equal on both sides. No hyper-resonance on one side and no dullness.

steps.do: Listen to air entry and added sounds over both lungs, comparing side to side
steps.find: Widespread polyphonic expiratory wheeze over both lungs with a prolonged expiratory phase. Air entry reduced but present and equal on both sides; this is not a silent chest. No crackles, no bronchial breathing, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, no added sounds.

steps.do: Check for ankle oedema and feel the calves for tenderness or swelling
steps.find: No ankle oedema. Calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling on either side.

bedside.find: Not done yet. He is too breathless to do a reliable one; try again once he has settled. Do not hold up treatment to get one.
Sinus tachycardia at 116/min, regular, no ectopics or arrhythmia.
Sinus tachycardia 116/min, normal axis, normal intervals. No ST changes, no right heart strain pattern.
6.0 mmol/L.
92% on room air and drifting down from 93% at triage. Comes up to about 95% if oxygen is started.

amsa-583.key: Jeff has severe acute asthma. He cannot finish sentences, he is using his accessory muscles with a tracheal tug, and his SpO2 is 92% and getting worse. He has no life-threatening features: he is alert, not exhausted or cyanosed, and still has air entry, so this is not a silent chest. Equal resonant percussion with equal breath sounds argues against a pneumothorax. No urticaria, angioedema, stridor or hypotension argues against anaphylaxis. Soft calves, a normal JVP, no oedema and a normal ECG make PE and a cardiac cause unlikely.

amsa-599.vitals: HR 84 regular, BP 138/84 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C. Weight 92 kg (practice record 3 months ago: 97 kg), height 165 cm, BMI 34 kg/m².
amsa-599.general: Alert, friendly but flat in mood, comfortable at rest. Obese, with clothes looking a little loose. Smells of cigarette smoke. Not jaundiced or short of breath, and no obvious cachexia.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and fingers for clubbing, koilonychia, pallor of the palmar creases and nicotine staining.
steps.find: Nicotine staining of the right index and middle fingers. No clubbing, no koilonychia, palmar creases normal colour.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae for pallor and the sclerae for icterus.
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. No scleral icterus.

steps.do: Inspect the teeth, mucosa, tongue and oropharynx with a torch.
steps.find: Good dentition, moist mucous membranes. No oral ulcers, candida or masses.

steps.do: Ask her to say 'ah' and watch the palate, ask her to stick out her tongue, and listen to her voice.
steps.find: Palate rises symmetrically, tongue protrudes midline with no wasting or fasciculation, voice normal.

steps.do: Watch her take a sip of water.
steps.find: Swallows without coughing, choking or any change in voice.

steps.do: From behind, palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes, including the left supraclavicular fossa (Virchow's node), and the thyroid.
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, including the left supraclavicular fossa. Thyroid not enlarged. No neck mass.

steps.do: Auscultate the lungs and heart.
steps.find: Mildly reduced air entry throughout, no crackles or wheeze. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs.

steps.do: Inspect, then palpate for tenderness, an epigastric mass, the liver and the spleen, and percuss for shifting dullness.
steps.find: Obese, soft and non-tender. No epigastric mass. Liver and spleen not palpable. No ascites.

steps.do: Check facial symmetry and speech, and limb power, sensation and reflexes.
steps.find: No facial asymmetry or dysarthria. Normal power, sensation and reflexes in all four limbs.

bedside.find: 92 kg today against 97 kg three months ago: about 5 kg (5%) unintentional loss.
5.8 mmol/L (normal).
Normal: no blood, protein, glucose, ketones, leucocytes or nitrites.

amsa-599.key: Samantha has lost 5 kg (about 5% of her body weight), confirmed against her practice record, and has mild conjunctival pallor. Together with progressive dysphagia to solids, these are alarm features for oesophageal cancer and she needs an urgent gastroscopy. Her mouth, lower cranial nerves, water swallow and neurological screen are all normal, which fits oesophageal rather than oropharyngeal dysphagia. She also has no Virchow's node, epigastric mass, hepatomegaly or ascites, so there are no clinical signs of spread.

amsa-625.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 96% on room air, BP 162/88 mmHg (right arm), HR 86/min regular, temperature 36.8 °C, alert, pain 5/10
amsa-625.general: Overweight woman sitting on the edge of the trolley with her right leg hanging over the side and a sock still on the right foot. Uncomfortable but alert and chatty. Nicotine staining of the right index and middle fingers. If she is asked to lie flat, the pain gets worse within a minute ("Oh, that's worse, I need to hang it down") and eases once the leg is hanging down again.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, feel the radial pulse for rate and rhythm, and measure BP in both arms
steps.find: Nicotine staining of the right index and middle fingers. Radial pulse 86/min and regular. BP right arm 162/88 mmHg, left arm 158/86 mmHg, so the arms are equal.

steps.do: Auscultate the praecordium and listen over both carotids
steps.find: Dual heart sounds with no murmurs. No carotid bruits.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen for a pulsatile or expansile aortic mass
steps.find: Soft. No pulsatile or expansile mass.

steps.area: Inspection of the legs and feet
steps.do: Explain why, remove the right sock, and inspect both legs and feet, including between the toes and the heels
steps.find: Both shins are hairless with thin, shiny skin. Right foot: the great, second and third toes are black, dry and shrivelled, and the blackening extends onto the medial forefoot over the first metatarsal head, with a sharp line of demarcation. The fourth toe is dusky blue. The rest of the foot is pale, shiny and hairless, and the toenails are thickened. No discharge, redness, swelling or smell, and no heel ulcer. With the leg hanging down, the right foot is dusky red. Left foot: no ulcers, no gangrene, nothing between the toes.

steps.do: Compare the temperature of both feet with the back of the hand, and test toe capillary refill
steps.find: Right foot cold to the mid-foot; left foot cool. Capillary refill more than 5 seconds in the right fourth and fifth toes, and 3 seconds in the left toes.

steps.do: Palpate the femoral (and auscultate for bruits), popliteal, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both sides
steps.find: Femoral pulses palpable on both sides, the right weaker, with a right femoral bruit. Popliteal: right absent, left palpable. Right dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial both absent. Left dorsalis pedis weak; left posterior tibial palpable.

steps.do: Raise each leg to find the angle at which the foot goes pale, then hang it over the side of the bed
steps.find: The right foot goes white at about 15 degrees, then slowly turns deep red over about 30 seconds when hung down. The left foot goes pale at about 50 degrees. This means severe ischaemia on the right. Lying flat makes her pain worse.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both calves for swelling, warmth and tenderness, and compare their size
steps.find: Soft, non-tender and equal in size. Not warm, with no swelling or redness.

steps.do: Test monofilament sensation, vibration sense, power and ankle reflexes
steps.find: Reduced monofilament sensation over both forefeet. Vibration reduced at the left great toe and at the right medial malleolus; the right great toe cannot be tested because it is gangrenous. Power 5/5 throughout. Ankle reflexes reduced on both sides.

steps.do: Palpate the spine, assess flexion and perform a straight leg raise
steps.find: Not tender, with full flexion. Straight leg raise negative on both sides.

bedside.find: Requested. The result will be given in Part 2.
11.2 mmol/L
Sinus rhythm at 86/min, regular, with no AF and no acute ischaemic changes

amsa-625.key: Petunia has dry gangrene of the right first three toes and medial forefoot, and her fourth toe is threatened. She also has absent right popliteal and pedal pulses, a cold foot, delayed capillary refill and a Buerger's angle of about 15 degrees. Together with 3 weeks of rest pain that is eased by hanging the leg down, this is chronic limb-threatening ischaemia with tissue loss, and it needs same-day vascular escalation even though all her observations are normal. Her regular rhythm makes an embolic cause less likely, and the lack of redness, discharge or smell means there is no foot infection. Her soft calves and normal spine argue against DVT and spinal stenosis, and her coexisting diabetic neuropathy matters for protecting the foot.

amsa-626.vitals: HR 124 beats/min regular, BP 132/84 mmHg (right arm) and 130/82 mmHg (left arm), RR 26 breaths/min, SpO2 92% on room air, temperature 37.8 °C, alert (14:40 set; the 08:00 set was all normal)
amsa-626.general: Sitting up in bed. Anxious and mildly short of breath at rest, but speaking in full sentences. Alert. Not sweaty, not cyanosed and not pale. No respiratory distress beyond a raised respiratory rate.

steps.do: Inspect the hands for cyanosis and pallor, feel the radial pulses on both sides at the same time, and assess rate and rhythm
steps.find: Warm hands with no peripheral cyanosis. Radial pulse 124 beats/min, regular, and equal on both sides with no radio-radial delay.

steps.do: Measure the blood pressure in both arms
steps.find: 132/84 mmHg in the right arm and 130/82 mmHg in the left. No significant difference between the arms, so nothing suggests dissection, and he is not hypotensive.

steps.do: Assess the JVP at 45 degrees and check the position of the trachea
steps.find: JVP not raised. Trachea midline.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the praecordium, then listen to all areas for heart sounds, murmurs and a pericardial rub, including with him sitting forward
steps.find: Apex beat not displaced. Heart sounds dual and tachycardic with no murmur and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Inspect for work of breathing, then assess chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the front and back of the chest
steps.find: Mildly increased work of breathing at rest. Chest expansion equal. Resonant to percussion throughout. Vesicular breath sounds throughout with no crackles, wheeze or pleural rub. No signs of pneumothorax, consolidation or effusion.

steps.do: Palpate over the sternum, costal cartilages and ribs, especially the right lower chest, and look for bruising or deformity
steps.find: No tenderness anywhere, so the pain cannot be reproduced. No bruising or deformity. The pain is not musculoskeletal.

steps.do: Inspect and compare both legs. Palpate for warmth, tenderness along the deep veins and pitting oedema. Measure both calves 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity and feel the peripheral pulses
steps.find: The right calf is swollen, red and warm, and tender along the deep veins. The right calf measures 4 cm more than the left. Pitting oedema of the right ankle and shin. The left leg is normal. Peripheral pulses present and equal.

steps.do: Inspect the surgical wound and dressings
steps.find: Clean and dry with intact dressings. No redness, swelling or discharge.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen, including the epigastrium
steps.find: Soft and non-tender with no epigastric tenderness.

bedside.find: Sinus tachycardia at 124 beats/min with a normal axis and normal intervals. No ST elevation or depression and no T wave inversion. No RBBB, S1Q3T3 or right ventricular strain. Compared with the pre-operative ECG, only the rate has changed.
6.1 mmol/L (normal)

amsa-626.key: Five days after hip surgery, he has new tachycardia, tachypnoea, hypoxaemia and a low-grade fever, with a normal BP. Together with a swollen, red, tender right calf that is 4 cm larger than the left, this strongly suggests a DVT that has caused a pulmonary embolism, and his Wells score is high. The rest of the examination is normal: clear chest, no rub, no chest wall tenderness, equal BP in both arms, and an ECG showing sinus tachycardia only. This makes pneumonia, pneumothorax, pericarditis, musculoskeletal pain, aortic dissection and ACS less likely. Because his BP is normal, he is haemodynamically stable.

amsa-630.vitals: HR 134 bpm regular, BP 88/60 mmHg, RR 28 breaths/min, SpO2 91% on room air (94% if high-flow oxygen has been given), Temp 36.6 °C, CRT 3 seconds, pain 7/10, GCS 15
amsa-630.general: A 20-year-old man of athletic build (about 72 kg). He is sitting upright on the trolley, holding his left side, and is clearly breathless and distressed. He is using his neck and shoulder muscles to breathe and can only speak in short sentences. He is not cyanosed. He is not on supplemental oxygen unless the candidate has asked for it. He is on a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place. There are grazes on his left arm and left thigh. He says it is worse when he lies flat.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill and look for peripheral cyanosis
steps.find: Cool peripheries. Capillary refill 3 seconds. No peripheral cyanosis. Grazes on the left forearm.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and note the BP
steps.find: Radial pulse 134 bpm, regular and weak (low volume). BP 88/60 mmHg.

steps.do: Inspect the neck veins and palpate the trachea in the sternal notch
steps.find: Neck veins distended. Trachea deviated to the right.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the chest wall for bruising, wounds, tenderness, crepitus, surgical emphysema and paradoxical movement
steps.find: Bruising and an abrasion over the left lateral chest. Tender over the left lateral ribs. No crepitus, no surgical emphysema, no flail segment and no open or sucking wound.

steps.do: Assess chest expansion on both sides and percuss both hemithoraces from front to back
steps.find: Reduced expansion on the left. Hyper-resonant to percussion over the whole left chest. Normal expansion on the right, which is resonant.

steps.do: Auscultate both lungs, front and back
steps.find: Breath sounds reduced over the whole left lung. Right lung: vesicular breath sounds with no added sounds. No wheeze on either side.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart sounds
steps.find: Heart sounds present and not muffled. Tachycardic with no murmur and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the abdomen, including the left upper quadrant for splenic injury
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, including the left upper quadrant. No guarding and no bruising. Well-healed appendicectomy scar.

steps.do: Assess conscious level and palpate the cervical spine
steps.find: Alert, GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). No cervical spine tenderness. Moving all four limbs normally.

steps.do: Inspect the legs for injury and examine the calves for DVT
steps.find: Grazes on the left thigh. Calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling.

bedside.find: Sinus tachycardia at 134 bpm. Normal axis, no ST or T wave changes, no low voltage and no electrical alternans.
7.1 mmol/L
7/10, left lateral chest, worse on breathing in

amsa-630.key: This is a left tension pneumothorax causing obstructive shock. He has distended neck veins and a trachea pushed to the right. His left chest moves less, is hyper-resonant and has reduced breath sounds, and he is hypotensive, tachycardic and hypoxic. The heart sounds are clear, which points away from tamponade. The left chest is hyper-resonant rather than dull, and the neck veins are full rather than flat, which points away from haemothorax. Rib tenderness alone cannot explain the shift or the shock. This is a clinical diagnosis, so it needs high-flow oxygen, a senior doctor and immediate left-sided decompression now, without waiting for the chest X-ray.

amsa-631.vitals: RR 46/min, SpO2 93% on room air, HR 158/min regular, BP 96/60 mmHg, temperature 37.8 °C, central CRT 2 seconds, alert (AVPU A), weight 15 kg (triage at 06:40: RR 44, SpO2 94%, HR 155, BP 98/62)
amsa-631.general: Alert 3-year-old boy, a bit grizzly but settles on his mother's lap. Sitting upright and breathing fast. Talking in short sentences, a little less than usual for him. Pink, not cyanosed. Clear nasal discharge. No drooling, no stridor, normal voice. Not tripoding. Well grown (15 kg, about the 65th centile).

steps.do: Counts the respiratory rate and looks for tracheal tug, subcostal and intercostal recession, nasal flaring, accessory muscle use, head bobbing and grunting
steps.find: RR 46/min. Moderate subcostal and intercostal recession with some abdominal breathing. No tracheal tug, no nasal flaring, no head bobbing, no grunting.

steps.do: Inspects chest shape and symmetry, checks tracheal position and chest expansion
steps.find: Chest looks slightly hyperexpanded. Trachea central. Expansion equal on both sides.

steps.do: Percusses both sides of the chest, front and back
steps.find: Resonant throughout on both sides. No dullness.

steps.do: Listens to both lungs, front and back, comparing sides for air entry and added sounds
steps.find: Widespread high-pitched expiratory wheeze on both sides with a prolonged expiratory phase. Good, equal air entry on both sides; not a silent chest. No focal crackles, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Checks heart rate and rhythm, peripheral temperature and central capillary refill, and listens to the heart
steps.find: HR 158/min, regular. Warm peripheries, central CRT 2 seconds. Heart sounds normal, no murmur.

steps.do: Checks mucous membranes, eyes and skin turgor
steps.find: Lips slightly dry, tongue moist, eyes not sunken, normal skin turgor. Not clinically dehydrated.

steps.do: Inspects the skin for urticaria, angioedema, petechiae and eczema
steps.find: Dry, slightly rough eczema patches in both elbow and knee creases. No urticaria, no lip, face or tongue swelling, no petechiae or purpura.

steps.area: Ears, nose and throat, and neck
steps.do: Examines the throat and ear drums and feels the cervical lymph nodes
steps.find: Clear nasal discharge. Mildly red throat, tonsils not enlarged, no exudate. Ear drums normal on both sides. A few small, soft, non-tender cervical lymph nodes.

steps.do: Palpates the abdomen
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No masses, no organomegaly.

bedside.find: SpO2 93% on room air at 06:55 (94% at triage). Above 92%, so no oxygen is needed yet. Trend is slightly worse.

bedside.test: Reassessment 20 minutes after salbutamol 6 puffs (100 microgram/puff) by spacer and mask, if given
bedside.find: RR 40/min, SpO2 95% on room air, HR 156/min. Less recession, but mild subcostal recession and wheeze remain. A little more settled. Heart rate still fast because of the salbutamol; otherwise improving.

bedside.test: Nasopharyngeal swab for respiratory viral PCR
bedside.find: Taken at triage and sent to the lab. The result will be given in Part 2.

bedside.test: Chest X-ray or bloods, if asked for
bedside.find: Results will be given in Part 2 (not routinely indicated).

amsa-631.key: Wesley has a moderate episode: he is alert, has moderate subcostal and intercostal recession, talks in short sentences and has SpO2 93–94% in air, with widespread bilateral expiratory wheeze and good, equal air entry. This fits viral-induced wheeze and needs salbutamol by spacer now, with senior review because his observations are in the yellow zone and getting slightly worse. Several findings argue against the dangerous differentials: no urticaria or angioedema (against anaphylaxis), symmetrical signs with no focal crackles or bronchial breathing (against an inhaled foreign body or pneumonia), and no stridor or drooling (against croup or epiglottitis). He is well perfused and not clinically dehydrated.

amsa-632.vitals: Repeat set at 10:50 on room air: RR 34/min, SpO2 86% on room air, HR 114/min regular, BP 212/112 mmHg, Temp 36.8 °C, capillary refill 3 s, alert (A on AVPU), BGL 7.2 mmol/L (triage 10:42: RR 32, SpO2 87%, HR 108, BP 206/108). Weight 88 kg. With oxygen, SpO2 rises to about 92%. After GTN, BP falls to about 160/90 mmHg and HR to about 104/min.
amsa-632.general: 73-year-old man sitting bolt upright on the trolley, in severe respiratory distress. He is using his neck and shoulder muscles to breathe and can only say 3 or 4 words at a time. He is sweaty and frightened, with dusky lips. A tissue in his hand holds pink frothy sputum. He is on a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place. He will not lie flat: "Don't lie me down, I can't breathe flat."

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and peripheral stigmata
steps.find: Cool and clammy hands, capillary refill 3 seconds. No clubbing. Nicotine staining of the right fingers. Small healed puncture mark at the right wrist (radial angiogram access).

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and compare both sides
steps.find: 114/min (about 104/min after GTN), regular, normal volume. No radio-radial delay.

steps.do: Check the blood pressure (manual or from the monitor)
steps.find: 212/112 mmHg before treatment (about 160/90 mmHg after GTN). Severely hypertensive.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for cyanosis, then assess the JVP with him sitting upright
steps.find: Dusky lips. JVP raised, 5 cm above the sternal angle with him sitting upright.

steps.do: Inspect, then palpate for the apex beat, heaves and thrills
steps.find: Apex beat displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No parasternal heave, no thrills. No chest wall trauma.

steps.do: Auscultate all four valve areas, listening for added sounds, murmurs and a rub
steps.find: S1 and S2 with an added third heart sound (gallop rhythm). No murmurs. No pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check tracheal position, chest expansion, percussion and auscultation front and back (sitting forward with support, keeping him upright)
steps.find: Trachea central. Expansion reduced at both bases. Dull to percussion at both bases, resonant above. Breath sounds reduced at both bases. Fine inspiratory crackles over both lungs from the bases up to the mid zones. No wheeze, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness, the liver and an aortic mass
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. Liver not palpable. No pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the lumbar spine and paraspinal muscles, and check for sacral oedema
steps.find: Tender lumbar paraspinal muscles. No midline bony tenderness. No sacral oedema.

steps.do: Check both ankles for pitting oedema, the calves for DVT and the foot pulses
steps.find: Trace pitting oedema at both ankles. Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling. Foot pulses present on both sides.

bedside.find: 7.2 mmol/L
Regular narrow complex tachycardia at about 110 to 114/min, no ectopics seen
Room air SpO2 86%, rising to about 92% on titrated oxygen, but he is still very breathless
Pink, frothy, watery sputum in the tissue. Not purulent, no frank blood.

bedside.test: 12-lead ECG, venous blood gas and bloods
bedside.find: ECG recorded and bloods with a venous gas sent. The examiner will give the results in Part 2.
Requested. The examiner will give the report in Part 2.

amsa-632.key: He has severe, worsening hypoxaemic respiratory distress (RR 34 and SpO2 86% on room air) with marked hypertension. He needs sitting upright, oxygen to a target of 92 to 96%, nitrates and senior help straight away. The raised JVP, S3, displaced apex, bilateral crackles to the mid zones and bibasal dullness (effusions) point to acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema from left ventricular failure after his recent MI. The afebrile, regular rhythm, clear sputum and soft calves argue against pneumonia, AF and PE.

amsa-633.vitals: RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 128/78 mmHg, HR 104 bpm regular, temperature 38.6 °C, alert, pain 8/10, BGL 6.1 mmol/L. Weight 88 kg, height 165 cm (BMI about 32).
amsa-633.general: Uncomfortable, lying still on the trolley and avoiding movement. Flushed and sweaty. Alert and oriented. Obese body habitus. IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, feel the temperature of the peripheries and check capillary refill
steps.find: Warm peripheries, CRT 2 seconds. No stigmata of chronic liver disease (no palmar erythema, leuconychia, clubbing or asterixis).

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae and skin for jaundice and the mucous membranes for hydration
steps.find: Sclerae not yellow, no jaundice. Mucous membranes slightly dry. No spider naevi or scratch marks.

steps.do: Inspect the exposed abdomen with the patient lying flat
steps.find: Not distended, moves normally with breathing. Healed appendicectomy scar in the right iliac fossa. No visible masses.

steps.do: Palpate all nine regions, starting away from the pain and watching her face
steps.find: Marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant with voluntary guarding. Mild epigastric discomfort. No tenderness elsewhere. No rebound tenderness, no rigidity. No masses.

steps.do: Press below the right costal margin in the mid-clavicular line while she breathes in, then compare the left side
steps.find: Murphy's sign positive: she stops breathing in when the gallbladder area is pressed. No catch on the left.

steps.do: Palpate for the liver, gallbladder, spleen and kidneys
steps.find: Liver not enlarged. Gallbladder not palpable. Spleen and kidneys not palpable.

steps.area: Percussion and auscultation of the abdomen
steps.do: Percuss for tenderness and shifting dullness, then listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: No percussion tenderness away from the right upper quadrant. No shifting dullness. Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.do: Press over the renal angles and check the inguinal and femoral hernial orifices
steps.find: Renal angles not tender. Hernial orifices normal.

steps.do: Check chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the lungs including the right base, then auscultate the heart
steps.find: Equal expansion, resonant, clear breath sounds including the right base. Dual heart sounds, no murmurs.

steps.do: Offer a rectal or pelvic examination
steps.find: The examiner says it is not needed.

bedside.find: 6.1 mmol/L
Sinus tachycardia 104/min, no ST or T wave changes.
Negative for blood, leucocytes, nitrites and bilirubin.
Bloods have been sent; results and the ultrasound are given in Part 2.

amsa-633.key: Fever of 38.6 °C, tachycardia, and right upper quadrant tenderness with guarding and a positive Murphy's sign point to acute cholecystitis rather than biliary colic. She has no jaundice and no signs of generalised peritonitis, and her BP and perfusion are normal, so she is septic-looking but not shocked. A clear right lung base, a normal ECG, a negative urine dipstick and non-tender renal angles make pneumonia, ACS and a renal cause less likely.

amsa-634.vitals: HR 108 bpm regular, BP 118/76 mmHg, RR 18 breaths/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 37.4 °C, BGL 5.8 mmol/L
amsa-634.general: Uncomfortable woman lying on the trolley. With each wave of cramping pain she curls up and stops talking, then settles between waves. Bilious green-yellow vomit in the bowl beside her. Alert and talking in full sentences.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes, check capillary refill centrally and peripherally, and feel the temperature of the peripheries
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes. CRT 2 seconds. Warm peripheries.

steps.do: Look for pallor, jaundice and stigmata of chronic disease, and palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes, including Virchow's node
steps.find: No pallor, no jaundice. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Expose the abdomen from nipples to knees with the patient lying flat. Look for distension, scars and visible peristalsis
steps.find: Mildly distended. Well-healed Pfannenstiel scar and a right iliac fossa (gridiron) scar. No visible peristalsis.

steps.do: Examine the inguinal, femoral and umbilical regions and both scars for incisional hernia, with a cough impulse
steps.find: No inguinal, femoral, umbilical or incisional hernia. Cough impulse negative.

steps.do: Palpate gently, watching her face, then deeply across all regions for tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound, masses and organomegaly
steps.find: Mild diffuse tenderness, worst around the umbilicus. No guarding, rigidity or rebound tenderness. No masses. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.

steps.do: Percuss across the abdomen and test for shifting dullness
steps.find: Tympanic centrally. No shifting dullness.

steps.do: Auscultate for bowel sounds for at least 30 seconds
steps.find: High-pitched, tinkling bowel sounds.

steps.do: Request a PR examination with consent and a chaperone
steps.find: Empty rectum. No blood on the glove. No mass felt.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lungs
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, tachycardic. Chest clear with good air entry on both sides.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L
She has not passed urine since she arrived, so no sample is available yet. Serum beta-hCG has been sent with the bloods (result in Part 2).
Small residual volume, about 80 mL, consistent with low urine output rather than retention.
Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Normal axis and intervals, QTc normal. No ischaemic changes.

amsa-634.key: The findings that matter are tinkling bowel sounds, a mildly distended tympanic abdomen and bilious vomiting in a woman with Pfannenstiel and gridiron scars. Together these point to small bowel obstruction, most likely from adhesions. Her tachycardia and dry mucous membranes show significant fluid loss. The normal hernial orifices and the absence of guarding, rigidity or rebound make an incarcerated hernia or established strangulation less likely. They do not rule out ischaemia, so she needs close re-examination.

amsa-635.vitals: HR 96 regular, BP 132/80 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 37.8 °C, BGL 5.6 mmol/L (triage set at 10:40)
amsa-635.general: Tired, irritable 40-year-old man who keeps scratching his arms and chest. Visibly jaundiced. Alert and fully oriented to time, place and person. Speaking in full sentences, not distressed at rest, well perfused.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms, then test for asterixis with the arms outstretched and wrists dorsiflexed
steps.find: No clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. No asterixis.

steps.do: Inspect the skin of the trunk and limbs and both antecubital fossae for injection sites
steps.find: Raised, red, blanching wheals (urticaria) over the trunk and limbs, with scratch marks. A few healing puncture marks in the left antecubital fossa, with no abscess, cellulitis or thrombophlebitis. No spider naevi, bruising or petechiae.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae in good light and check conscious state and orientation
steps.find: Yellow sclerae (scleral icterus). Alert and fully oriented, with no confusion or drowsiness.

steps.do: Inspect for gynaecomastia and loss of body hair, and palpate the cervical, supraclavicular and axillary nodes
steps.find: No gynaecomastia and normal body hair. No lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect and move the large and small joints, including the knees and wrists
steps.find: Knees and wrists ache on movement. No swelling, warmth or effusion.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen with the patient lying flat
steps.find: Not distended. No caput medusae, scars or visible veins.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply, palpate the liver and spleen, test Murphy's sign, ballot the kidneys and check for guarding and rebound
steps.find: Tender in the right upper quadrant. The liver edge is smooth, soft and tender, 3 cm below the right costal margin. Murphy's sign negative. No guarding or rebound. Spleen not palpable and kidneys not ballotable.

steps.do: Percuss the liver span, test for shifting dullness and listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Liver span 15 cm. No shifting dullness. Normal bowel sounds.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and the lung fields, including both bases
steps.find: Normal heart sounds with no murmurs. Chest clear at both bases.

steps.do: Perform a digital rectal examination and inspect the glove
steps.find: Pale, clay-coloured stool on the glove. No blood or melaena.

bedside.find: Dark, tea-coloured urine. Bilirubin 2+. No blood, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.6 mmol/L
Sinus rhythm at 96/min, normal axis and intervals, no ST or T wave changes.
Results will be given in Part 2.

amsa-635.key: Andrew is jaundiced with a low-grade fever, urticaria, and a smooth, tender liver 3 cm below the costal margin. Murphy's sign is negative, the urine contains bilirubin and the stool is pale, which together point to acute hepatitis rather than gallbladder disease. Fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice make up Charcot's triad, so cholangitis still has to be ruled out in Part 2. He is alert with no asterixis, a normal BGL and no stigmata of chronic liver disease, so there is no sign of acute liver failure or chronic liver disease. The healing puncture marks in his left antecubital fossa back up the needle-sharing history as the likely route of infection.

amsa-663.vitals: HR 84 bpm regular, BP 122/76 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C, weight 70 kg (75 kg two months ago), height 178 cm, BMI 22.1 kg/m²
amsa-663.general: Alert, friendly young man, comfortable at rest and not distressed. Slim build. Not pale or jaundiced. Well hydrated: moist mucous membranes, normal skin turgor. Not short of breath. No drip, stoma or other equipment.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for clubbing, palmar pallor, leuconychia and palmar erythema; check capillary refill.
steps.find: No clubbing, no palmar pallor, no leuconychia. Capillary refill under 2 seconds. Normal.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae and sclerae for redness (episcleritis, uveitis), conjunctival pallor and jaundice.
steps.find: No redness or injection, no conjunctival pallor, no scleral icterus. Normal.

steps.do: Inspect the oral mucosa, tongue and gums for aphthous ulcers, angular stomatitis and hydration.
steps.find: No mouth ulcers. Moist mucous membranes. Normal.

steps.do: Expose and inspect the abdomen lying flat for distension, scars, visible masses and stomas.
steps.find: Not distended, no scars, no visible masses. Normal.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all nine regions, watching his face; check for guarding and rebound; palpate and percuss for the liver and spleen; ballot the kidneys; check the renal angles.
steps.find: Soft. Mild tenderness in the left iliac fossa, with no guarding or rebound. No masses. Liver and spleen not palpable. Renal angles not tender. Percussion note normal, no shifting dullness.

steps.do: Listen for bowel sounds.
steps.find: Bowel sounds present and normal. Not tinkling, not absent.

steps.do: Expose and inspect both lower legs; palpate any lesions for tenderness, size, warmth and ulceration; look elsewhere for pyoderma gangrenosum.
steps.find: Four tender, raised, red-purple nodules 1 to 3 cm across over both anterior shins, with no ulceration. Consistent with erythema nodosum. No other rashes or skin ulcers.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the small joints of the hands, the knees and the ankles for swelling, warmth and tenderness.
steps.find: No swelling or tenderness of the hands, knees or ankles. Normal.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lung fields.
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs. Chest clear with good air entry on both sides. Normal.

steps.area: Perianal inspection and digital rectal examination
steps.do: Explain and get consent, offer a chaperone, position him in the left lateral position; inspect the perianal region, then perform a digital rectal examination and inspect the glove.
steps.find: No skin tags, fissures, fistulae or abscess. Rectum mildly tender, no mass felt. Blood and mucus on the glove.

bedside.find: 70 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 22.1 kg/m². About 5 kg (7%) lost from 75 kg over 2 months.
Lying 122/76 mmHg, HR 84; standing 120/78 mmHg, HR 88. No postural drop, no symptoms.
No blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites, glucose or ketones. Normal.
5.4 mmol/L (random). Normal.

amsa-663.key: Andy has lost 5 kg, his left iliac fossa is mildly tender, and there is blood and mucus on the glove, with no perianal disease. Together with tender nodules on both shins (erythema nodosum), this points to inflammatory bowel disease affecting the distal bowel, and the absence of skin tags, fissures or fistulae makes Crohn's disease less likely. He has no fever, no tachycardia and no peritonism, is not pale and is well hydrated, so there are no signs of acute severe colitis and he can be investigated and managed as an outpatient.
